<!-- source=github_issue; title=NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object; url=https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2 -->

# NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2

With the Unity 2022 Editor update I get:
NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
LipsyncToAnim.Convert () (at Assets/LipsyncToAnim/LipsyncToAnim.cs:83)
LipsyncToAnim.OnValidate () (at Assets/LipsyncToAnim/LipsyncToAnim.cs:53)
UnityEngine.GUIUtility:ProcessEvent(Int32, IntPtr, Boolean&)
after clicking convert. Used it a bunch on 2019 with no problems.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: AdalynBlack | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 9 | url: https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2#issuecomment-1855937772
It looks like Oculus's OVR Lipsync package may have been updated
I'll have a look at it and try to update it
Comment 2 | author: AdalynBlack | association: OWNER | reactions: 2 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2#issuecomment-2143222141
So sorry I haven't worked on this for a while. I've been busy with school and such for a while now, but I should be free to fix the problem now. It might be a day or two before I get a chance to take a look, but I'll definitely have a look when I have a chance
Comment 3 | author: AdalynBlack | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2#issuecomment-2143235974
I'm trying to recreate the issue on my end and it seems to work just fine. Could you verify the issue with a fresh project and installation, using the latest version of the OVRLipSync package? The core of the issue seems to be related to OVRLipSync failing to generate any lipsync data for the input audio from what I can tell
Comment 4 | author: AdalynBlack | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 11 | url: https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2#issuecomment-2143256350
I see
could you try the demo scene, and if that fails, could you try cloning the git repo and upgrading it to Unity 2022?
Comment 5 | author: AdalynBlack | association: OWNER | reactions: 2 | score: 13 | url: https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2#issuecomment-2143263605
ohh I found the issue
Enable "Preload Audio Data" on the audio file. Newer Unity versions seem to import with that disabled by default. I'll push a fix that loads the data if it's not already loaded
Comment 6 | author: AdalynBlack | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 9 | url: https://github.com/AdalynBlack/LipsyncHelper/issues/2#issuecomment-2143266964
Ok, this issue is now officially resolved. As of Version 0.2.3, the script will now load the audio if it isn't already loaded

Hi, I just wanted to let you know that while trying to make my own sensor plugins, I was able to solve this problem. The main issue was the dependency on ROS2 package `image-transport-plugins` which can be installed with `sudo apt install ros-${ROS_DISTRO}-image-transport-plugins` and also the 'camera_info' topic for both RGB and Depth camera was mismatched which can be solved by the naming convention you suggested above.
I'm very happy that i got it working finally. I haven't tested the GPS yet but i'll let you know if i do.
Thank you.

Comment 6 | author: ma11088 | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/zolantris/ValheimMods/issues/50#issuecomment-1933644898
> Can you tell me where to look for it? I used the Object search and typed "SailComponent" but nothing showed up. Only when searching with "Sail" stuff pops up
Just had to restore an old world to replicate the problem, but I am positive that this is what I did, keeping in mind that I did this locally and then uploaded it to my server once I confirmed it was fixed:
Enter the world. Check with Bepin to see your error text is appearing, as it would be.
Object Explorer > Search UnityObject > Class Filter: (I just type sail and then select the following) "valheimraft.sailcomponent" > Select MBSail > in the window that pops up, select "Inspect Game Object" > Click "Destroy"
Save the world, log out or exit, start it up again and confirm that your world isn't giving you the errors, reupload to server.

<!-- source=github_issue; title=XPortal crashes on dedicated server with Valheim Plus installed; url=https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/29 -->

# XPortal crashes on dedicated server with Valheim Plus installed

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/29

**Describe the bug**
- I have installed Xportal to a dedicated server running Valheim Plus only (Server side). Since installing (March 8th) I have had to fly around the map to "remap" the portals. I am unsure as to why, but the portal names are reverting back to nothing which means there is nothing to also select for a destination.
**To Reproduce**
- Install Valheim Plus and XPortal on dedicated server
- Run the server
- A player joins the server
- XPortal (on the server) will now receive a sync request, this is where the error occurs (in `XPortal.KnownPortal.GetColour()`).
**LogOutput file(s)**
- ~~[LogOutput.log](https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/files/10937134/LogOutput.log)~~
- [LogOutput.log](https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/files/10937490/LogOutput.log)
**Version**
- 1.2.6
**Environment**
- Dedicated Server
**Other mods**
- Jotunn 2.10.4
- Valheim Plus 0.9.9.11
**Priority**
- Medium
---
Edits by @SpikeHimself :
### Updated summary (2023-03-28)
- As soon as a player joins, the server is trying to build a list of all portals so that it can send that to the player. This immediately goes wrong, because the server is failing to retrieve the portal colour:
```
[Info :XPortal.RPC] Received sync request from `206028287` because: Achilliez (206028287) has joined the game
[Info : Unity Log] 03/09/2023 17:07:21: Exception in ZRpc::HandlePackage: System.Reflection.TargetInvocationException: Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation.
---> System.Reflection.TargetInvocationException: Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation.
---> System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
at XPortal.KnownPortal.GetColour (UnityEngine.GameObject prefab)
at XPortal.KnownPortal.GetPortalColour (ZDOID portalId)
at XPortal.KnownPortal..ctor (ZDOID id)
at XPortal.KnownPortalsManager.UpdateFromZDOList (System.Collections.Generic.List`1[T] zdoList)
at XPortal.XPortal.ForceLocalPortalUpdate (System.Collections.Generic.List`1[T] allPortals)
at XPortal.XPortal.ProcessSyncRequest (System.String reason)
at XPortal.RPC.RPC_SyncRequest (System.Int64 sender, System.String reason)
```
In v1.2.6 this error could occur if the portal prefab does not have child GameObject `_target_found_red/Point light` or that child does not have a `Light` component:
https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/blob/0af97be809fea73263e416d24760c071644a4a43/XPortal/KnownPortal.cs#L24-L28
Newer versions of XPortal have improved logging so that we can determine the precise cause, but this was not yet tested by this issue's author.
**We do know that removing ValheimPlus resolves the issue.** Therefore this is a compatibility issue.
---
### Steps to take to help with testing
* Download the latest [Debug release](https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/releases) of XPortal
* [Enable debug logging](https://github.com/SpikeHimself/resources/wiki/BepInEx:-Enable-debug-logging) in your BepInEx config
* Install Valheim Plus and the latest Debug release of XPortal on a dedicated server
* Run the server with a world that already has portals (or create one first)
* Join the server
* Share the server's `LogOutput.log`

<!-- source=github_issue; title=GitHub Desktop will not launch, for unclear reasons; url=https://github.com/desktop/desktop/issues/3443 -->

# GitHub Desktop will not launch, for unclear reasons

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/desktop/desktop/issues/3443

### Description
I'm trying to install and run GitHub Desktop. Yesterday I spent two hours trying to just install the software, the process goes as follows:
1. Launch the GitHubDesktopSetup.exe file (latest one available from the website).
2. The installer frame pops up that says "GitHub Desktop is installing and will launch when it's finished."
3. The installer frame disappears and nothing happens.
Results:
- I have a process running in the background called "GitHubDesktop.exe".
- I can now see "GitHub Desktop" in my control panels "Programs & Features"/"Uninstall Program".
- I get the folders for GitHub Desktop in AppData/Local and AppData/Roaming.
- I cannot launch the application, even if I end the process already running.
Attempting to re-install by following these steps:
1. End all processes that might still be running.
2. Uninstall the application via "Programs & Features"/"Uninstall Program" in the Control Panel.
3. Manually delete the "GitHub Desktop" folders in AppData/Local and AppData/Roaming.
4. Reboot my PC.
5. Attempt another installation, that follows above mentioned process.
This cycle repeats for each time I attempt to install GitHub Desktop.
Yesterday, after two hours of repeating this process and troubleshooting via Google, it finally worked for some reason. I did not do anything different than the process explained.
When it worked, I was able to get started working on my project in Unity, using GitHub as version control.
Today, I launched GitHub Desktop to start working on my project again and it doesn't launch. I tried rebooting my PC, I tried ending the process and launching the application again - to no avail.
Finally, I decided to reinstall it. Now I'm currently repeating the same old cycle described above and the application will not even install or launch.
Literally nothing appears after the installer frame shows up for <1 second.
### Version
Latest version available from the website as of 28th November 2017.
### Operating System Version
Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.16299.64]
### Steps to Reproduce
Explained above in the Description.
**Expected behavior:** GitHub Desktop to install and launch properly.
**Actual behavior:** Nothing. At all.
**Reproduces how often:** 99% - I can't say 100% since it for some reason worked once yesterday and then stopped working.
### Logs
There is no "logs" folder.
#### Additional Information
N/A.

Thanks for your reply!

I attached the requested logfile above.
I would like to add that it did in fact install after a few hours of repeating the process described in the original post. I'm currently using it for the second day in a row.
When googling for solutions I found some reply mentioning something about how a WiFi network can affect the installation and the times when GitHub Desktop has failed to launch (even though it worked at home) and the installer has failed (as described in the original post) has been when I'm in school on the _eduroam_ wifi network. Maybe this has something to do with it?

Comment 3 | author: shiftkey | association: MEMBER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/desktop/desktop/issues/3443#issuecomment-348017656
@Saxmax well that log file doesn't show anything bad happening during the install. And I'm glad to see that it is working now.
> When googling for solutions I found some reply mentioning something about how a WiFi network can affect the installation and the times when GitHub Desktop has failed to launch (even though it worked at home) and the installer has failed (as described in the original post) has been when I'm in school on the eduroam wifi network. Maybe this has something to do with it?
This sounds like the behaviour of the classic Windows application - we chose an installer technology that was just the bootstrapper, which would then require network access to download the files when installing. The new Electron-based app doesn't require the network to install.
> If it stops working again I will try to install it from my home network instead to see if it runs smoothly then, but this could prove tedious as I will need to fix it even if I am in school.
Please keep us posted. It might be that the installer completed but the first launch of the application didn't succeed, but I've not heard of another report like that so far. Event Viewer might have some interesting errors but as I've not been able to trigger this myself I'm not sure what specifically to look for.

I've reset my computer now (using Windows 10's system reset feature) and will attempt using GitHub Desktop again when Unity Collab terminates their free licesense (9th January, I think).
Comment 6 | author: ArTDsL | association: NONE | reactions: 2 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/desktop/desktop/issues/3443#issuecomment-1227686753
Solve to me:
1. Go to: `%AppData%\..\Local\GitHubDesktop`
2. You should see something like this:
![github folder](https://i.imgur.com/UlfPlBe.jpg)
3. In my case i have 3 versions that is `app-3.0.3`, `app-3.0.5` and `app-3.0.6`
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10051552/186751695-ca52997f-c3a3-4ad2-8185-2a26aca2fc7f.png)
4. Select the updated bug version (in my case was the `app-3.0.6`) and delete the folder.
5. Select the last version you are using ***before the bug occurs*** (in my case was the version `app-3.0.5`), open the folder and double-click on `GitHubDesktop.exe`, **open** the app **and close it**.
6. Go back to `GitHubDesktop` main folder (`%AppData%\..\Local\GitHubDesktop`), and run the `Update.exe` wait at least 10 secs.
7. Execute the `GitHubDesktop.exe` on main folder (`%AppData%\..\Local\GitHubDesktop`).
8. When you open the app a notification should pop up saying that you need to restart your Github Desktop to install the last updates, i didn't use the message, i click on the `X` on right corner and just close the app.
9. Just execute the github desktop like you always do on your computer.
**When you open the app everything should be back to normal again!**
_I'm sorry to bring this post back to life (lucky tha way i'm) i got stuck in same problem, but i found this solution, hope my voice can help some lost soul on their journey!_

<!-- source=github_issue; title=Teleport Marker doesn't survive scene change; url=https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1388 -->

# Teleport Marker doesn't survive scene change

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1388

## Overview
Running a project with multiple scenes, when a new scene is loaded the Mixed Reality Teleport Script loses its reference to the initial instance of Teleport Marker instantiated in the first scene. The Teleport Manager doesn't survive the scene load and a new one isn't created in the new scene.
## Expected Behavior
No errors, can select using Controller
## Actual Behavior
Three errors, xbox controller no longer functions, can't select or interact
```
MissingReferenceException: The variable teleportMarker of MixedRealityTeleport doesn't exist anymore.
You probably need to reassign the teleportMarker variable of the 'MixedRealityTeleport' script in the inspector.
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.EnableMarker () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:285)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.StartTeleport () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:214)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.HandleGamepad () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:124)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.Update () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:103)
MissingReferenceException: The object of type 'Animator' has been destroyed but you are still trying to access it.
Your script should either check if it is null or you should not destroy the object.
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.PositionMarker () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:316)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.Update () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:109)
MissingReferenceException: The variable teleportMarker of MixedRealityTeleport doesn't exist anymore.
You probably need to reassign the teleportMarker variable of the 'MixedRealityTeleport' script in the inspector.
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.DisableMarker () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:298)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.FinishTeleport () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:236)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.HandleGamepad () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:129)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.MixedRealityTeleport.Update () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/MixedRealityTeleport.cs:103)
```
## Steps to reproduce
Create a project with two scenes. Load initial scene then load second scene. Use xbox left thumbstick.
You can see that the Mixed Reality Teleport Script on MixedRealityCameraParent in the Unity Editor is null.
## Unity Editor Version
2017.2.op1-MRTP4
## Mixed Reality Toolkit Release Version
master
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: genereddick | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1388#issuecomment-345326257
TeleportMarker is instantiated in the MixedRealityTeleport script Start function.
```
private void Start()
{
...
if (teleportMarker != null)
{
teleportMarker = Instantiate(teleportMarker);
teleportMarker.SetActive(false);
animationController = teleportMarker.GetComponentInChildren<Animator>();
if (animationController != null)
{
animationController.StopPlayback();
}
}
}
```
Because this script is on the MixedRealityCameraParent which has DontDestroyOnLoad, the Start function is only called on the first scene load. The teleportMarket is created in the first scene, but doesn't survive the scene load and it doesn't look like there is a mechanism to reinstantiate it in new scenes.
Comment 2 | author: cvasquez-github | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1388#issuecomment-346189186
Using Unity 2017.2.0p1 - MRTP4 64bit + HoloToolkit-Unity-v1.2017.2.0
I have another issue when changing scene, controllers disappear.
Throws exception on line 496 of InputManager.cs, **sourceStateEventData** is null on next scene.
```
NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.InputManager.RaiseSourceDetected (IInputSource source, UInt32 sourceId, System.Object[] tags) (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/Managers/InputManager.cs:496)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.InteractionInputSource.OnEnable () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/InputSources/InteractionInputSource.cs:189)
```
Comment 3 | author: genereddick | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1388#issuecomment-347028269
Actually it is not enough to just add don't destroy on load. Property assignments don't necessarily survive scene loading. In this case, even though the Teleport Marker now survives the scene load, the value of teleportMarker does not:
private GameObject teleportMarker;
Which is assigned in the MixedRealityTeleport.cs script Start function:
if (teleportMarker != null)
{
teleportMarker = Instantiate(teleportMarker);
When you load a new scene that value is now null as are some other properties. I'm still not totally clear on which values survive scene loads -- static values on all objects, behavior of properties on objects with dontdestroyonload, nested gameobjects all seem to have different rules. -- but I expect this issue and others related to multi-scene projects are going to continue to cause problems unless addressed across all singletons.
So here, in addition to adding DontDestroyOnLoad to the the TeleportMarker.prefab, you also need to add some code to reset the reference when the new scene is loaded. This applies to animationController as well.
Comment 4 | author: genereddick | association: NONE | reactions: 4 | score: 11 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1388#issuecomment-347035932
Three options:
1. Instantiate TeleportMarker as a child of MixedRealityCameraParent. Then doesn't require DontDestroyOnLoad, but not sure of any implications of tying the position and rotation of the TeleportMaker to the camera.
2. Make TeleportMarker a Singleton. Will both survive the scene load and will retain the reference in MixedRealityTeleport.
3. Add some code to handle rewiring the object in MixedRealityTeleport. This could be done either through re Instantiating the TeleportMarker (in which case it doesn't need DontDestroyOnLoad), or just use Find to grab it and reassociate it (if TeleportMaker has DontDestroyOnLoad).
In MixedRealityTeleport.cs:
private void Awake() {
SceneManager.sceneLoaded += SceneLoaded;
}
void SceneLoaded(Scene scene, LoadSceneMode mode) {
if (teleportMarker != null) {
teleportMarker = Instantiate(teleportMarker, this.transform);
teleportMarker.SetActive(false);
animationController = teleportMarker.GetComponentInChildren<Animator>();
if (animationController != null) {
animationController.StopPlayback();
}
}
}
Comment 5 | author: Maximiliankk | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1388#issuecomment-360912328
Found a quick fix for this. I put this in MixedRealityTeleport.cs:
public void LoadMarker()
{
teleportMarker = Resources.Load("TeleportMarker") as GameObject;
animationController = teleportMarker.GetComponent<Animator>();
}
and then I have a small script on an empty object in the scene that is being switched to with this:
private void Awake()
{
GameObject.Find("MixedRealityCameraParent").GetComponent<MixedRealityTeleport>().LoadMarker();
}
I also set the script execution order so this will be earlier than the others, but i'm not sure if this is necessary or not.

Unity log link: https://pastebin.com/E13azkEn
Mod Loader log link: https://pastebin.com/z9qktrzx
Works fine on MelonLoader v0.2.7.4, UnityExplorer v3.1.12.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: sinai-dev | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 11 | url: https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/issues/54#issuecomment-817100117
Ok it went a bit deeper than I thought but I'm pretty sure I fixed it. Let me know how this release goes for you https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/releases/tag/3.3.11
Comment 2 | author: sinai-dev | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/issues/54#issuecomment-817106821
Hmm ok, upon further inspection it seems that MelonLoader is not unstripping the `UnityEngine.UI.dll` module.
Could you try with BepInEx instead?
- Move/backup the `version.dll` file in the game folder. Put it inside the MelonLoader folder or whatever.
- Download [BepInEx 6 IL2CPP x64](https://builds.bepis.io/projects/bepinex_be/359/BepInEx_UnityIL2CPP_x64_b45d90b_6.0.0-be.359.zip)
- Extract this zip into the game folder, so it looks like `Wasteland 3\BepInEx\...` and `Wasteland 3\winhttp.dll`
- Download [this 2019.4.4.zip](https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/files/6289575/2019.4.4.zip)
- Create a folder `BepInEx\unity-libs\`
- Extract the 2019.4.4 zip into the `unity-libs` folder
- Run the game, it may take 20 secs or so while BepInEx unstrips the libraries
Hopefully this works, otherwise I'm afraid I'm not sure we'll get much further.
Comment 3 | author: sinai-dev | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/issues/54#issuecomment-817108875
Is that from your first launch with BepInEx? I don't see any unstripping going on in the BepInEx log.
Well, not too sure what else to try, we need to get the unstripped UnityEngine.UI to be loaded somehow. Could you try just dropping this file into your `BepInEx\unhollowed\` directory? (and unzipping it)
[UnityEngine.UI.dll.zip](https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/files/6289602/UnityEngine.UI.dll.zip)
Comment 4 | author: sinai-dev | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/issues/54#issuecomment-817110564
Hmm, that's odd, I'm setting the ColorBlock essentially the same way with 3.1.12 - https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/blob/12cd718f12cf35eaee7964940123de8fbd191fb9/src/UI/UIFactory.cs#L83
Strange that this doesn't throw the same exception then. I'll download the 2019.4.4 editor and have a look myself.
Comment 5 | author: sinai-dev | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/issues/54#issuecomment-817285453
Update again: Finally figured out what's going on here.
The issue is simply that I am creating the UI too quickly. Looks like this game is doing some stuff to destroy all GameObjects on startup, so I just need to wait a second or so for that.
Fix will be pushed shortly.
Comment 6 | author: sinai-dev | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 11 | url: https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/issues/54#issuecomment-817287100
Fixed :) https://github.com/sinai-dev/UnityExplorer/releases/tag/3.3.12

<!-- source=github_issue; title=Exceptions thrown when playing via Holographic Remote Player; url=https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/4575 -->

# Exceptions thrown when playing via Holographic Remote Player

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/4575

## NullReferenceException in GGVPointer.OnPreSceneQuery
When following the 'getting started with MRTK Guide' and opening the HandInteractoinExamplesScene or any other scene, an exception is thrown when gazing upon an Item. Playing the Scene via Holographic Remoting Player.
## To reproduce
**Prequesites**
- download and import MRTK Foundation and Examples packages (v2.0.0 RC1 Refresh)
- download and insall Holographic Remoting Player on HoloLens 1
- Set Unity Target Platform to UWP
- In XR settings, enable Virtual Reality, add MRTK to list
**Steps**
1. Create a new Scene in Unity
2. Top Panels > Mixed Reality Toolkit > Add to Scene and Configure
3. Add a Cube GameObject
4. Properly scale and place the object in the scene
translation: `x: 0; y: 0; z:2;`
scale: `x: 0.2; y: 0.2; z: 0.2;`
5. Create and add a script containing the following:
`using Microsoft.MixedReality.Toolkit.Input;`
`public class CubeSelector : MonoBehaviour, IMixedRealityInputHandler`
`void IMixedRealityInputHandler.OnInputDown(InputEventData eventData){/*any simple functionality*/}`
`void IMixedRealityInputHandler.OnInputUp(InputEventData eventData){/*any simple functionality*/}`
## Expected behavior
When gazing upon a selectable item (Cube in custom scene or any object in the HandInteractionExamples demo scene) and selecting it by gesture, the defined selection behaviour should apply.
## Screenshots
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15180559/58417298-aa237680-8084-11e9-8d7e-fad89cb26832.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15180559/58417320-bd364680-8084-11e9-97f1-ba7474caf553.png)
In GGVPointer.cs:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15180559/58417366-ea82f480-8084-11e9-9d1e-1b9d96c25a7e.png)
## Your Setup (please complete the following information)
- Unity Version [e.g. 2018.3.14f1]
- MRTK Version [e.g. v2.0.0 RC1 Refresh]
## Target Platform (please complete the following information)
- HoloLens
## Additional context
I am just getting started with HoloLens development (moreover I'm completely alone so noone can help me with their experience). When running examples in the editor everything works as expected (except that I have to click 2-3 times before the interaction is recognized. When using the holographic remoting player, and playing any scene via HoloLens(1), I get a crash either upon gaze or AirTap Gesture.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: Weasy666 | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 6 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/4575#issuecomment-496247222
It's the same for me with every kind of input on the HoloLens 1.
My setup is:
Unity 2019.1.4f1
MRTK v2.0.0-RC1-Refresh (Foundation + Examples)

I believe I fixed this issue in https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/pull/4380 a week or so ago, but it hasn't been cut into a particular release yet.
You could also just code directly from that change and patch it in locally.
The underlying issue appears to be a regression in Unity or Unity's WMR packages, so the fix that we adopted here is merely a workaround.

<!-- source=github_issue; title=NullReference Exception on Startup When Using DataBus with Existing StructureMap Child Container; url=https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968 -->

# NullReference Exception on Startup When Using DataBus with Existing StructureMap Child Container

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968

When starting an endpoint, a NullReferenceException occurs if the following conditions are met:
1. Using StructureMapBuilder with an existing container that happens to be a StructureMap child container (as distinguished from an NServiceBus child container which is a StructureMap nested container)
2. Using the DataBus feature
I have been able to reproduce this with NServiceBus 6 both with the generic host and when self-hosted.
NServiceBus 6.4.0
NServiceBus.Host 7.0.2
NServiceBus.StructureMap 6.0.0
StructureMap 4.5.2
I had previously successfully used child containers with Unity, but have recently switched to StructureMap and started encountering this error.
A minimal repro of this problem can be found at: https://github.com/dennismsmith/NServiceBusStructureMapDataBusError
Note that the order of initializing the DataBus and the container doesn't matter; the error occurs in both cases. If you switch the container to not be a child container, NServiceBus will start correctly, but that breaks some other use cases in my application.
The stack trace is as follows:
`2017-09-22 08:31:29.380 FATAL NServiceBus.GenericHost Exception when starting endpoint.

Comment 1 | author: timbussmann | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 8 | url: https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968#issuecomment-331443276
hey @dennismsmith
Thanks a lot for the repro sample 👍 It indeed seems to be related to the child container. The IDataBus implementation registered by the `DataBusFileBased` feature doesn't seem to be resolved correctly.
@Particular/container-maintainers can you chime in?
Comment 2 | author: boblangley | association: MEMBER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968#issuecomment-331593475
@timbussmann Correct. The DataBus property is not being injected.
@dennismsmith StructureMap does not support using setter injection policies defined in a child container: https://github.com/structuremap/structuremap/issues/596#issuecomment-317722797. NServiceBus still uses setter injection to populate dependencies, which requires NServiceBus.StructureMap to [create those policies](https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus.StructureMap/blob/develop/src/NServiceBus.StructureMap/ConfigurationExpressionExtensions.cs#L11) for each type registered in the container it is using.
Comment 3 | author: timbussmann | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 5 | url: https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968#issuecomment-331852378
@boblangley if we change https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/blob/develop/src/NServiceBus.Core/DataBus/DataBus.cs#L48 to use ctor injection, this would solve this specific exception. While this still means that we don't support property injection in that case (because that's a structuremap issue), it should allow to use a child container as mentioned by @dennismsmith ?
Comment 4 | author: boblangley | association: MEMBER | reactions: 0 | score: 9 | url: https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968#issuecomment-331884004
@timbussmann Should we check downstreams to see if any rely on setter injection and fix those as well?
Comment 5 | author: dennismsmith | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968#issuecomment-332852418
@timbussmann: The reason that we are using child containers is that we are self-hosting multiple endpoints in the same process. We register all of our general application configuration in the parent container, and then create a child container for each endpoint. When we started self-hosting multiple endpoints in the same process in NServiceBus 5 using Unity, we found the the endpoints would insert conflicting mappings into the container. I don't remember the exact details of what the conflicts we saw were since we made those changes several years ago.
Comment 6 | author: mauroservienti | association: MEMBER | reactions: 0 | score: 9 | url: https://github.com/Particular/NServiceBus/issues/4968#issuecomment-332882277
Another possible approach is to switch to a container, such as Castle.Windsor, that supports child containers and constructor injection and property injection on the same resolved conponent

# Installers not being run before injected method on monobehaviour in latest verison?

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/ssannandeji/Zenject-2019/issues/122

I am not sure if I am doing something wrong but I have a MB based class which looks like so:
```
public class Something : MonoBehaviour
{
[Inject]
public ISomething Here {get;set;}
[Inject]
public void OnceTheAboveIsInjected()
{ ... }
}
```
And I have some installers in the scene which registers `ISomething` and if I put a debug log after binding it I can see it is within the container, however whenever it tries to inject into `Something` class it blows up saying it cannot resolve type `ISomething`, I put a debug output just before the throw on line 787 and it seems to be getting called before the installers have finished running.
I couldnt find a `[PostInject]` attribute in the new version and it looked like `[Inject]` was to be used for that purpose so I cannot see anything wrong with what I am doing here, so is there anything quirky I need to know about this stuff? I thought all installers would complete before MBs would have their injections occur.

public class AppContainer : EcsRxContainer

viewEntity.AddComponent(new CameraFollowsComponent());
}
}
```
There is a base class that looks like:
```
public abstract class EcsRxContainer : MonoBehaviour
{
[Inject]
public ISystemExecutor SystemExecutor { get; private set; }
[Inject]
public IPoolManager PoolManager { get; private set; }
protected List<IEcsRxPlugin> Plugins { get; private set; }
protected EcsRxContainer()
{
Plugins = new List<IEcsRxPlugin>();
}
[Inject]
private void Init(DiContainer container)
{
RegisterAllPluginDependencies(container);
SetupAllPluginSystems(container);
SetupSystems();
SetupEntities();
}
protected abstract void SetupSystems();
protected abstract void SetupEntities();
protected virtual void RegisterAllPluginDependencies(DiContainer container)
{ Plugins.ForEachRun(x => x.SetupDependencies(container)); }
protected virtual void SetupAllPluginSystems(DiContainer container)
{
Plugins.SelectMany(x => x.GetSystemForRegistration(container))
.ForEachRun(x => SystemExecutor.AddSystem(x));
}
protected void RegisterPlugin(IEcsRxPlugin plugin)
{ Plugins.Add(plugin); }
}
```
So it is looking for the specifically bound type... OH or are you saying because its bound to `ISystem` not the explicit concrete type it wont find it?

Strangely enough, I've heard this from almost everyone with initial problems. It kine of resolved itself?!?! That's what I've also seen when someone sent me a project. I opened it and then it worked, sent it back, and it worked :) Yay.

Comment 4 | author: sschmid | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/sschmid/Entitas/issues/495#issuecomment-348025570
Once the project is loaded by roslyn, there shouldn't be any `could not resolve` warnings anymore when using `entitas client gen`. The client/server completely replaced `gen -a`, it's more flexible and can be easily send from anywhere (e.g. from IDE or Unity). In case you have issues with the client on windows, I'm currently rewriting the tcp sockets (used for communicating between client and server) to make it work on windows
Comment 5 | author: sschmid | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/sschmid/Entitas/issues/495#issuecomment-350115575
@gabrjt looks like you're using the reflection-based code gen in the terminal. If so, you have to update your searchpaths to point to the Unity dlls
(taken from [Match One - Entitas.properties](https://github.com/sschmid/Match-One/blob/master/Entitas.properties))
```
${user.unity}/Managed, \
${user.unity}/Managed/UnityEngine, \
```
or even easier, just generate in Unity.
If you're using roslyn, you will not have this issue, but then keep in mind, you can only generate from the terminal like described in this video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LGKsqSg5FHg
Comment 6 | author: optimisez | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/sschmid/Entitas/issues/495#issuecomment-350201438
Hi @sschmid, I think I found the root cause of the problem. As stated in issue #503, when you open the project the in Visual Studio it will generate ```<TargetFrameworkProfile>Unity Subset v3.5</TargetFrameworkProfile>``` in [Your project name].csproj and cause the Roslyn code generator cannot work properly. When u open the project with Visual Studio, it will generate different .csproj file. Open with Visual Studio will generate [Your project name].csproj meanwhile MonoDevelop will generate Assembly-CSharp.csproj. I'm using Unity 2017.2 and Visual Studio 2017. I attached that 2 .csproj files for you to inspect.
[Unity Test Project.csproj.txt](https://github.com/sschmid/Entitas-CSharp/files/1541932/Unity.Test.Project.csproj.txt)
[Assembly-CSharp.csproj.txt](https://github.com/sschmid/Entitas-CSharp/files/1541933/Assembly-CSharp.csproj.txt)

Regarding the sign-in behavior, the recommended behavior is to attempt to Sign-In Silently first (that way your user doesn't have to sign-in again every time you get into that scene) and if that fails, Sign-In should be called instead.
As for the Connected Storage, the best sample (if you're using this Unity-Plugin) is to look at the :
'GameSave' Folder > Examples. That example scene shows the 'GameSaveUI' prefab which is actually an example of how to use 'GameSaveHelper', the actual script that you can use to integrate with Connected Storage.

# Weird `ExecutionEngineException: String conversion error: Illegal byte sequence encounted in the input` on Windows

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/KSP-ModularManagement/KSPe/issues/32

Fellow Kerbonaut [Astraph](https://forum.kerbalspaceprogram.com/index.php?/profile/80902-astraph/) is being throw under the bus by a pretty weird Exception:
```
[ERR 16:54:46.309] Couldn't extract exception string from exception of type TargetInvocationException (another exception of class 'ExecutionEngineException' was thrown while p

I don't have the slightest idea about what this can be, but I'm guessing that some String on an Assembly Metadata is *kaput*, and by trying to handle something related to such Assembly KSP is caught with its pants down.

Comment 1 | author: Lisias | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/KSP-ModularManagement/KSPe/issues/32#issuecomment-1244470401
There's very good chance that we may be dealing with an environmental problem (or, at least, trigger).
So I made this thing : [ksp-offline-check.zip](https://github.com/net-lisias-ksp/KSPe/files/9551768/ksp-offline-check.zip) ([source on this repo](https://github.com/KSP-ModularManagement/KSPe/tree/mestre/Source/ksp-offline-check)).
In order to use it, one need to unzip it somewhere and then:
```
./ksp-offline-check.exe DLL ~/Workspaces/KSP/runtime/1.12.3 ~/Workspaces/KSP/runtime/1.7.3
```
Where, obviously, `~/Workspaces/….` should be replaced by the pathname of your KSP's rigs you wanna test (yeah, you can run it on more than one). If the pathname have spaces or similar weirdyties you need to use double quotes on the pathnames:
```
./ksp-offline-check.exe DLL "C:\\Programs Files\\Games\\KSP\\1.12.3" "C:\\Programs Files\\Games\\KSP\\1.7.3"
```

> AI Overview
>
> The error message "System.ExecutionEngineException: String conversion error: Illegal byte sequence encountered in the input." when using Harmony, often indicates an issue with character encoding, particularly when dealing with file paths containing non-ASCII characters.
>
> Here's a breakdown of the problem and potential solutions:
>
> Problem:
> This error typically arises when Harmony, a library used for patching and modifying code in .NET applications (common in modding for games like RimWorld or Kerbal Space Program), encounters a file path or other string that contains characters outside of the standard ASCII set (e.g., accented letters, special symbols). The underlying .NET runtime (often Mono in these contexts) has trouble converting these "illegal byte sequences" into a usable string format, leading to the String conversion error.
>
> Solutions:
>
> Relocate the game or mod files to an ASCII-only path:
>
> If the game or mod files are installed in a directory whose path includes non-ASCII characters (e.g., C:\Users\José\Games\MyGame), moving them to a path containing only standard English letters and numbers (e.g., C:\Games\MyGame) can resolve the issue. Verify mod installation and integrity.
Ensure that all mods are correctly installed and that no files are corrupted or missing. Re-downloading and reinstalling problematic mods might be necessary. Check mod load order (if applicable).
In games that use a mod load order, ensure that Harmony is loaded correctly, often before other core game files and expansions, as well as any mods that depend on it. Investigate specific mod requirements.
Some mods might have specific requirements or known incompatibilities that could contribute to this error. Consult the mod's documentation or community forums for guidance. Consider .NET runtime or Harmony updates.
In some cases, updating the .NET runtime or Harmony library to a newer version might include fixes for character encoding issues. This is more relevant for developers or advanced users.

Comment 6 | author: Lisias | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 13 | url: https://github.com/KSP-ModularManagement/KSPe/issues/32#issuecomment-4501553925
> > ... the subst stunt, I don't use it since the MS-DOS era
>
> :) Probably the code of subst.exe didn't change much from that time and it works somehow incorrectly with .NET applications.
Nope, the problem is the asinine way the .NET (or at least Mono) handles symlinks, junctions and mount points. This thing gets the absolute path of everything, completely screwing up the logical location of the files.
In order to be ensure the pathnames given to "my" IO subsystem are inside their sandbox, I need the logical paths (if not by other reason, because I do a lot of symlinks for the add'ons installed to save valuable space on SSDs), and so I "unreparse" these pathnames to their "original" form (black magic, essentially, and slow but the results are cached for the rest of the session).
I completely forgot that `subst` still exist - so this use case of yours are more than welcome, because if you use it, almost surely someone else also does and I want you guys covered (assuming you aren't already).
**NOW**... Our real problem is why in hell the `ksp-offline-check` thingy is borking on you, because it is vanilla, vanilla, using the runtime's System.IO directly without any shenanigan of mine.
I will build a test bed here to investigate it. In time, you are using Windows 10 or 11? I'm currently only have access to a Windows 10 rig, so I will probably need your help to be sure about any findings.

# Duplicate Mediators

- Source: github_issue

I ran into this in the past once in a test scene and forgot about it, but am now unfortunately running into it again in my current project.

Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: yourpalmark | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/strangeioc/strangeioc/issues/71#issuecomment-31686392
So in mapView in MediationBinder I added the following line:
```
if (mono.gameObject.GetComponent(mediatorType) != null)
return;
```
before
```
MonoBehaviour mediator = mono.gameObject.AddComponent(mediatorType) as MonoBehaviour;
```
This fixed my issue, but there is probably some underlying issue on why I'm getting here.

public class AudioBuffer : MonoBehaviour
{
#region Singleton
private static AudioBuffer _instance;
private static bool _instanceInit = false;
public static AudioBuffer Instance
{
get
{
if (!_instance) _instance = FindObjectOfType<AudioBuffer>();
if (!_instance && !_instanceInit)
{
var audioBufferObject = new GameObject("AudioBuffer");
_instance = audioBufferObject.AddComponent<AudioBuffer>();
}
return _instance;
}
}
#endregion
[SerializeField] private bool alwaysRecording;
[SerializeField] private AudioBufferConfiguration audioBufferConfiguration = new AudioBufferConfiguration();
[SerializeField] private AudioBufferEvents events = new AudioBufferEvents();
public AudioBufferEvents Events => events;
private IAudioInputSource _micInput;
private RingBuffer<byte> _micDataBuffer;
private byte[] _byteDataBuffer;
private HashSet<Component> _activeRecorders = new HashSet<Component>();
public bool IsRecording(Component component) => _activeRecorders.Contains(component);
public bool IsInputAvailable => _micInput.IsInputAvailable;
public void CheckForInput() => _micInput.CheckForInput();
public AudioEncoding AudioEncoding => _micInput.AudioEncoding;
private void Awake()
{
_instance = this;
_instanceInit = true;
// Check this gameobject & it's children for audio input
_micInput = gameObject.GetComponentInChildren<IAudioInputSource>();
// Check all roots for Mic Input JIC
if (_micInput == null)
{
foreach (var root in gameObject.scene.GetRootGameObjects())
{
_micInput = root.GetComponentInChildren<IAudioInputSource>();
if (_micInput != null)
{
break;
}
}
}
// Use default mic script
if (_micInput == null)
{
_micInput = gameObject.AddComponent<Mic>();
}
InitializeMicDataBuffer();
}
private void OnEnable()
{
#if UNITY_EDITOR
// Make sure we have a mic input after a script recompile
if (null == _micInput)
{
_micInput = GetComponent<IAudioInputSource>();
}
#endif
_micInput.OnSampleReady += OnMicSampleReady;
if (alwaysRecording) StartRecording(this);
}
// Remove mic delegates
private void OnDisable()
{
_micInput.OnSampleReady -= OnMicSampleReady;
if (alwaysRecording) StopRecording(this);
_instanceInit = false;
}
// Callback for mic sample ready
private void OnMicSampleReady(int sampleCount, float[] sample, float levelMax)
{
events.OnMicLevelChanged.Invoke(levelMax);
var marker = CreateMarker();
Convert(sample);
if (null != events.OnByteDataReady)
{
marker.Clone().ReadIntoWriters(events.OnByteDataReady.Invoke);
}
events.OnSampleReady?.Invoke(marker, levelMax);
}
// Generate mic data buffer if needed
private void InitializeMicDataBuffer()
{
if (null == _micDataBuffer && audioBufferConfiguration.micBufferLengthInSeconds > 0)
{
var bufferSize = (int)Mathf.Ceil(2 *
audioBufferConfiguration
.micBufferLengthInSeconds * 1000 *
audioBufferConfiguration.sampleLengthInMs);
if (bufferSize <= 0)
{
bufferSize = 1024;
}
_micDataBuffer = new RingBuffer<byte>(bufferSize);
}
}
// Convert
private void Convert(float[] samples)
{
var sampleCount = samples.Length;
const int rescaleFactor = 32767; //to convert float to Int16
for (int i = 0; i < sampleCount; i++)
{
short data = (short)(samples[i] * rescaleFactor);
_micDataBuffer.Push((byte)data);
_micDataBuffer.Push((byte)(data >> 8));
}
}
public RingBuffer<byte>.Marker CreateMarker()
{
return _micDataBuffer.CreateMarker();
}
/// <summary>
/// Creates a marker with an offset
/// </summary>
/// <param name="offset">Number of seconds to offset the marker by</param>
/// <returns></returns>
public RingBuffer<byte>.Marker CreateMarker(float offset)
{
var samples = (int)(AudioEncoding.samplerate * offset);
return _micDataBuffer.CreateMarker(samples);
}
public void StartRecording(Component component)
{
StartCoroutine(WaitForMicToStart(component));
}
private IEnumerator WaitForMicToStart(Component component)
{
yield return new WaitUntil(() => null != _micInput);
yield return new WaitUntil(() => _micInput.IsInputAvailable);
_activeRecorders.Add(component);
if (!_micInput.IsRecording)
{
_micInput.StartRecording(audioBufferConfiguration.sampleLengthInMs);
}
if (component is IVoiceEventProvider v)
{
v.VoiceEvents.OnStartListening?.Invoke();
}
}
public void StopRecording(Component component)
{
_activeRecorders.Remove(component);
if (_activeRecorders.Count == 0)
{
_micInput.StopRecording();
}
if (component is IVoiceEventProvider v)
{
v.VoiceEvents.OnStoppedListening?.Invoke();
}
}
}
}

Comment 4 | author: keithbradner | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steamvr_unity_plugin/issues/311#issuecomment-461230055
Unfortunately, as it is, the binding ui shows information specific to the
headset you currently have connected. If you don’t have one connected it
can’t display anything. It loads this information from the SteamVR driver
specific to that headset.
I understand this isn’t necessarily intuitive, especially to devs that have
been working with SteamVR previously.
From your message I’m not clear on why you can’t have a headset connected
to do this.
Alternatively, you can manually edit the default JSON files (actions.json
and bindings) in the root of your project directory, open the binding ui,
and “save and generate”. It’s easier if you edit the jsons while the
project is closed but if you do it while it’s open be sure to go to
advanced and hit Refresh to load the new actions file.

# Non-ASCII characters are not displayed properly with TextMeshProUGUI and SoftMask.

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/mob-sakai/SoftMaskForUGUI/issues/216

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a TextMeshPro FontAsset with English font, and attach non-English font to its fallback list (I am using Noto Serif)
2. Create a Canvas with RenderMode set to Camera, and attach a Camera to it.
3. Create TextMeshProUGUI component under a SoftMask parent.
4. Non-English texts are not displayed correctly (see screenshots below).
**Expected behavior**
The texts should be displayed properly.
**Screenshots**
![Screenshot_0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28d4d726-23c3-4e21-8801-10d768f6f5f4)
^ English (Displaying properly)
![Screenshot_1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/280ef8af-d0e9-44a2-9b26-5020db82dd5e)
^ Traditional Chinese (Error)
![Screenshot_2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0babb91d-c4e2-4943-a659-a19b1454edb4)
^ Japanese (Error)
![Screenshot_3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64b35d9e-ae70-474e-9ed7-6618b3638ce2)
^ If I remove the SoftMask in Viewport, the error goes away.
![Screenshot_4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31406e7a-6b42-42c4-baa4-68962a1a1684)
^ Setting Masking Mode to Normal works correctly, as well as Anti-Aliasing.
![圖片](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a70fb3c8-d46f-4f0b-9d32-143a9deb91cd)
^ How the font is set up. The font itself is a static font with ASCII characters, with 3 fallback Japanese font (first 2 static, the last is dynamic fallback).
![Screenshot_5](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce0b9cfe-ba86-442e-8c8b-21a4b9a03d20)
^ Overlay causes error too; If I set the RenderCamera to overlay, the problematic texts disappear.
**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- Version 3.0.1
- Platform: Windows Editor
- Unity version: 6000.0.29f1
- Build options: [e.g. IL2CPP, .Net 4.x, LWRP]
- Unity 6 Text Mesh Pro Support is imported.
**Additional context**
I upgraded from 1.0.2, where the same error also existed.
UPDATE:
If I manually toggle on and off the "Ignore Children" option in Soft Maskable on the TextMeshProUGUI component, the texts starts rendering properly.
![圖片](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37c48298-5854-4892-9837-f8f26ae3d125)
^ Before toggle On
![圖片](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98ff8dd3-6bca-4b6b-ba93-0cd87c38bd48)
^ Toggle On
![圖片](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/103c04ea-db2b-428c-9fec-83b3306b88ff)
^ Toggle Off (texts start displaying properly.)

Comment 4 | author: mob-sakai | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/mob-sakai/SoftMaskForUGUI/issues/216#issuecomment-2558020076
As a workaround: by deactivating the relevant objects, they were displayed correctly.
<img width="388" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07c402cc-259a-4206-9cf9-4d14cf81ca80" />
Or, apply this patch: [UtilityHubMenuManager.patch.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18217618/UtilityHubMenuManager.patch.zip)
Comment 5 | author: mob-sakai | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/mob-sakai/SoftMaskForUGUI/issues/216#issuecomment-2558032668
By adding a delay before hiding the submenu, it was displayed correctly.
```
await UniTask.Delay(500, cancellationToken: CancellationToken.None);
await HideAllSubMenuAsync(0f, CancellationToken.None);
```
Considering the previous patch (calling `gameObject.SetActive(true)` after hiding the submenu), it seems that TextMeshProUGUI is processing "something" asynchronously when activated for the first time.
If we can find an accessible event that notifies when it completes, everything will be resolved!
Comment 6 | author: mob-sakai | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/mob-sakai/SoftMaskForUGUI/issues/216#issuecomment-2558286474

Comment 2 | author: ShadauxCat | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 6 | score: 17 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects/issues/2755#issuecomment-1802496423
Hi everyone! Thank you for reporting this issue. We are aware of this issue and it has actually already been fixed in our develop branch. A new 1.7.1 patch release will come out soon with this fix in it; however, as our internal release process takes a bit of time to get through, in the mean time, there is a workaround available to unblock you.
We made some changes to how we initialize RPCs in order to support their use within generic classes; unfortunately, we missed a test case in those changes (which is now included in our testing framework) that covers what is reported here. If a class with an RPC inherits from a class (other than NetworkBehaviour) without any RPCs, this issue will occur.
The workaround is to just put an RPC in the parent class. It doesn't have to be used anywhere, it just has to exist. It doesn't matter if it's a client RPC or a server RPC. For example, looking at the case reported in the issue description:
```csharp
public class Parent : NetworkBehaviour
{
}
public class Child : Parent
{
[ServerRpc]
public void TestServerRpc()
{
}
}
```
You can workaround the issue here like this:
```csharp
public class Parent : NetworkBehaviour
{
[ServerRpc]
public void WorkaroundDummyServerRpc()
{
}
}
public class Child : Parent
{
[ServerRpc]
public void TestServerRpc()
{
}
}
```
We apologize for the inconvenience and will try to get this fix put out as soon as we can, but in the mean time, the above pattern should be able to unblock you.
Comment 3 | author: zachstronaut | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects/issues/2755#issuecomment-1819861854
Hello!
1.7.0 also doesn't work for us because of this issue. Our codebase compiles fine under 1.6.0 but doesn't compile under 1.7.0.
We don't have any RPCs in the definitions of any generic NetworkBehaviour derivatives because of: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects/issues/714
That's the only limitation we've run into, and we've mitigated that with the suggested fix on issue 714.
The suggested fix here for this issue (2755) is a bit ambiguous, and also we have a LOT of classes with a LOT of RPCs so it'd be a bit of an undertaking if I'm understanding it correctly.
We have lots of generics and sub classes of generics, that may also themselves be generic. I thought it might be useful for you to see some examples of real inheritance chains we're using in our project:
```
Thing : NetworkBehaviour, IThing
AnotherThing : Thing
GenericThing<T> : AnotherThing
abstract AbstractThing<T> : GenericThing<T>
abstract SomeThing<T> : AbstractThing<T>, IThis, IThat
RealThing : SomeThing<FooType>
```
```
MyClass<A, B, C> : AnotherThing
MyThing : MyClass<Apples, Bananas, Coffee>
```
```
CompositeNetBehaviour<RootClass, ServerClass> : NetworkBehaviour
DooDad : CompositeNetBehaviour<DooDad, DooDadServer>, ILoveInterfaces
```
```
abstract NetModel : NetworkBehaviour
abstract NetModelBase : NetModel
abstract NetModelGeneric<TUI> : NetModelBase
MyNetModel : NetModelGeneric<MyUI>
```
Comment 4 | author: ShadauxCat | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 2 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects/issues/2755#issuecomment-1819867141
> I have tried the workaround but it doesn't seem to fix anything. If there is a chain of subclasses, does there need to one be in each class or just the top parent?
@gnovos Yes, it has to be every class in the chain. Basically if the codegen finds an RPC, it tries to generate a virtual method to initialize the RPCs and call the parent class's implementation. If the parent class has no RPCs, it will not have generated that virtual method, so the attempt to find and call it will fail with this error. And then when you add an RPC to the parent class, it will also generate this method, and will also try to call its own parent class's implementation, so then its parent also has to have an RPC in it, all the way up to NetworkBehaviour.
Comment 5 | author: ShadauxCat | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 4 | score: 14 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects/issues/2755#issuecomment-1819869184
@zachstronaut A NetworkBehaviour being generic is not actually relevant to the issue. Any NetworkBehaviour which has RPCs in it and derives from a parent class that does not have RPCs in it will trigger this error. As mentioned earlier, though, this issue is fixed in develop and we are in the process of trying to roll out a 1.7.1 with this fix ASAP. (Our internal release process limits how quickly we can get a release put out.)
Comment 6 | author: michalChrobot | association: MEMBER | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects/issues/2755#issuecomment-2504381968
Hi, I can see that the fix was included in [NGOv1.7.1](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects@2.1/changelog/CHANGELOG.html#181---2024-02-05:~:text=to%2010.0s.%20(%232710)-,%5B1.7.1%5D%20%2D%202023%2D11%2D15,-Add%20version%201.7.1) so I will close this issue

# ArgumentNullException and Failed to create Mujoco runtime

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues/1171

Hello, I had the same problem as issue #315 when trying out MuJoCo. In this case, I was trying to do the ball on the tilted plane stuff. I am currently testing it out on unity 2022.3.9f1 personal on Windows 10, using MuJoCo 3.0.1. The error was:
**"ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. Parameter name: native"**
Then followed by a spam of:
**"NullReferenceException: Failed to create Mujoco runtime. Mujoco.MjScene.StepScene () (at D:/..../mujoco/unity/Runtime/Components/MjScene.cs:345)"**
I have cloned a repository of the plugin from here: https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/tree/main, and manually imported the package from disk. Do I need the package to be on the same disk partitions? (As in I downloaded the package on D: and imported it from there, while my user directory was on C:).
Secondly, it is probably because I didn't understand some terms, but I did "Expand the zip archive to a directory called MuJoCo in your user directory, and copy the file MuJoCo\bin\mujoco.dll." By this does it mean that I should make a new user directory called "MuJoCo", or should it be automatically created like when I import the package? Because I manually created an empty MuJoCo folder directory for it.
Thirdly, what does it actually mean by "The library can also be copied into any location under your project’s Assets directory."? Does it mean that I have to manually copy paste the mujoco.dll file to the project's Assets directory? Or was there actually another way to do this?
Also lastly, the line "On Unity version 2020.2 and later, the Package Manager will look for the native library file and copy it to the package directory when the package is imported.". I was actually assuming this do be done, but after importing the plugin, a warning prompt appeared telling me there's no bin directory on the user directory, which is why I did it manually as implied on the second and third question.
Sorry for the lengthy question, but I hope my question can be solved so I can finally start exploring MuJoCo for my final year project. It may be something dumb on my part, but any kind of help is appreciated. Thank you.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: Balint-H | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues/1171#issuecomment-1795325114
> Secondly, it is probably because I didn't understand some terms, but I did "Expand the zip archive to a directory called MuJoCo in your user directory, and copy the file MuJoCo\bin\mujoco.dll." By this does it mean that I should make a new user directory called "MuJoCo", or should it be automatically created like when I import the package? Because I manually created an empty MuJoCo folder directory for it.
Yup this one is done manually.
> Thirdly, what does it actually mean by "The library can also be copied into any location under your project’s Assets directory."? Does it mean that I have to manually copy paste the mujoco.dll file to the project's Assets directory? Or was there actually another way to do this?
Its optional. Your project should have one reference to the mujoco.dll library, either placed in the package folder, or in your Assets folder (or subfolders).
> Also lastly, the line "On Unity version 2020.2 and later, the Package Manager will look for the native library file and copy it to the package directory when the package is imported.". I was actually assuming this do be done, but after importing the plugin, a warning prompt appeared telling me there's no bin directory on the user directory, which is why I did it manually as implied on the second and third question.
If you have manually copied the dll, it should be fine. I have yet to try Unity plugin with MuJoCo 3, but sometimes there is a bit of a lag before all issues with a release are ironed out on the Unity plugin side. You may want to downgrade to 2.3.7 (which I can verify works, if you downgrade, make sure the package and dll versions match). I'll eventually try to update to MuJoCo 3 in the near future, you could message in a week to check in?
Here's an example Unity project that has worked as fresh installs on multiple computers for me:

Let me know if this still does not work! If you can share a unity project repo where the issue is reproduced, I can take a look and see if there's anything that stands out.

<!-- source=github_issue; title=NullReferenceException when using SteamP2P Transport; url=https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122 -->

# NullReferenceException when using SteamP2P Transport

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122

I am using the SteamP2P Transport and have a simple setup for a lobby in unity. When trying to join a hosted game as a client, after a few seconds a NullReferenceException gets thrown in the NetworkManager.cs, at line 1144:
`MessagingSystem.ProcessIncomingMessageQueue();`
Then the `NetworkManager.Singleton.OnClientDisconnectCallback` is called, against what the `NetworkManager.Singleton.OnClientConnectedCallback` never gets called (so the client never connects properly).
Here are two threads, where people describe the similar problems:
1. [https://answers.unity.com/questions/1869491/messagingsystemprocessincomingmessagequeue-nullref.html?childToView=1870613](https://answers.unity.com/questions/1869491/messagingsystemprocessincomingmessagequeue-nullref.html?childToView=1870613)
2. [forum.unity.com/threads/anyone-have-sample-mlapi-with-steam-matchmaking.1098304/](https://forum.unity.com/threads/anyone-have-sample-mlapi-with-steam-matchmaking.1098304)
**I am using:**
- Unity 2020.3.20f1
- Netcode for GameObjects 1.0.0-pre.3
- Multiplayer Tools 1.0.0-pre.2
- SteamP2P Transport for Netcode for GameObjects 2.0.0
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: JamesMcGhee | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122#issuecomment-979351543
New [SteamNetworking Transport](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/tree/main/Transports/com.community.netcode.transport.steamnetworking) transport available in the community transports.
The new one **Does Not** ship [Steamworks.NET](https://github.com/rlabrecque/Steamworks.NET) with it so you would need to have [Steamworks.NET installed](https://github.com/rlabrecque/Steamworks.NET) such as from its author. They have Package Manager install instrucitons now as well.
Can you let me know if you have the same issue with it?
Its very similar to the older SteamP2P but cleans up a few things with how the Steam API is used and is no longer dependent on SteamManager which could be an issue in some cases if you had your own integration with Steam set up or where using a newer version of Steamworks.NET
This new approch also means you can be using the latest Steamworks.NET so that will help eliminate the issue being an old Steamworks.NET bug or a bug with the old SteamP2P transport's custom take on Steamworks.NET
Comment 2 | author: JamesMcGhee | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122#issuecomment-992969169
> Exactly the same issue here - I'm almost relieved to see that so many of you guys are also experiencing this to be honest..
>
> @JamesMcGhee this is what I was telling you about yesterday on the Heathen Engineering chat.
>
> Note that I've tried to provide the SteamNetworkingTransport component with the CSteamID to connect to manually (in the method triggered by the Evt Game Created event of the LobbyManager) but it didn't change anything.
My point was that the Steam P2P transport should be depricated and replaced by the
SteamNetworking transport listed here
https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/tree/main/Transports/com.community.netcode.transport.steamnetworking
This new transport is just a port of the older one but it updates the older one to work with modern version of Steamworks.NET
As far as a Null Ref I would have dig deeper into it honistly MLAPI / NetCode is its own beast we where simply looking to help port its old Steamworks based Steam P2P transport to use the modern flavor of Steamworks.NET
If you can proivide a stack trace as to where its breaking I might be able to take a guess as to what is going on ... assuming its Steamworks related and not somethign fundamental with MLAPI / NetCode
Comment 3 | author: JamesMcGhee | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122#issuecomment-996538966
Working with a developer on this issue from the point of view of Steamworks its self not the transport or MLAPI/NetCode directly.
Line 172 in the NetworkUpdateLoop.cs script is the point of failure for them ... it would seem that `NetworkUpdateStage` in the line
```csharp
RunNetworkUpdateStage(NetworkUpdateStage.EarlyUpdate)
```
Is null ... so anyone have idea as to why that would be null, e.g. where and when should it be initalized and how does it get this far as a null without being caught?
Is this something the transport should have initalized, or is this something the transport should have triggered the NetworkManager to initalize, etc.
We would need someone with more experience with MLAPI/NetCode for GameObjects to speak on these aspects
Comment 4 | author: JamesMcGhee | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122#issuecomment-1001620919
It will be some time before we can get back into the source code for this one
But, some tips if anyone else wants to take a swing at it
SteamNetworkingTransport.cs has a sub class in it
SteamNetworkingTransport.User
This is already tracked per user (hence the name) and holds the CSteamID and some ping info. You could likely just add a ulong unityId to that and update it when the user connects to do more or less what was done in change set [#1368](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects/pull/1368/files) from what I can see.
That said I haven't dove deep so not completly sure what is requried here just that I can see they are mapping IDs to each other and I do recall SteamNetworkingTransport already maintains a dictionary of user data
Comment 5 | author: LukeStampfli | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122#issuecomment-1006492416
Took me a while to figure this out. Debugging steamnetworking is still a real pain 😄. The issue wasn't in the IDs but the channel code which was incorrect.
#138 fixes the issue on my machine(s).
If anyone has time it would be great if you could test whether this version of the transport fully works as I only have a very simple sample project. Just add the following in the package manager via add by giturl:
```
https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions.git?path=/Transports/com.community.netcode.transport.steamnetworking#bdb9850f7d4d59a3b2a0eb224949966c5a131a03
```
Comment 6 | author: ElwoodHogan | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/multiplayer-community-contributions/issues/122#issuecomment-1047559873
I'm trying to implement the new fixes, but I'm still running into a few errors. Would it be possible to make a scene with a basic connection system implemented? I'm worried I've set something up wrong.

# Notarized MacOS app - Mediapipe dylib doesn't load/work

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/homuler/MediaPipeUnityPlugin/issues/616

### Plugin Version or Commit ID
v0.10.0
### Unity Version
2022.1.4f1
### Your Host OS
macOS Monterey 12.4
### Target Platform
Mac Standalone
### Command Sequences
python build.py build --desktop cpu--opencv cmake --solutions pose -vv
### Additional Context
Build runs correct when built directly and ran from Unity on MacOS, build also runs correctly once built to an Xcode project and ran from Xcode. Once the build has been archived and notarized successfully using the Apple Notarization service, the plugin doesn't load anymore, the build does open but mediapipe refuses to load or start.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: ROBYER1 | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/homuler/MediaPipeUnityPlugin/issues/616#issuecomment-1161782323
Just wanted to add as I investigate this, we had another issue where the OpenCV library library wasn't linked despite using the build command `python3 build.py build --desktop cpu --opencv cmake --solutions pose -vv`, builds would only work on the build machine due to the dynamic linking of OpenCV.
I can only attribute this to a build cache issue and cloned the repository fresh and rebuilt with the same command + copied the packages/com.homuler.. folder between projects and rebuilt the app which now works on other M1 mac machines.
I am currently waiting for the new app to be notarized and will report back if this issue is now fixed to help others.
In the build that wouldn't run, we had these errors:

Comment 2 | author: ROBYER1 | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 5 | url: https://github.com/homuler/MediaPipeUnityPlugin/issues/616#issuecomment-1161795032
Yep, I can confirm that the underlying issue was OpenCV not being statically linked, what threw us off was the errors above talk about DllNotFoundException: Unable to load DLL 'mediapipe_c' but the actual issue behind that error was that OpenCV was not bundled in the app and the app was looking for it at /opt/homebrew/opt/opencv@3/lib/
Once we used the build command in a fresh clone, rebuilt our app, notarized it and exported it to run, it runs!

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/ClearFoundry/ClearScript/issues/364

I'm trying to use ClearScript on HoloLens.
**What works:**
Clearscript works on Windows in Unity. For that I'm using the dlls from the .net-4.5-build-folder:
- Core.dll
- V8.dll
- Windows.Core.dll
- Windows.dll
- _win-x64.dll_
- _win-x86.dll_
**What does not work:**
The HoloLens runs on UWP and the architecture should be ARM64. So if I understand it right, a application running on the HoloLens should need the dlls from the uap-10.0-build-folder (there are only those two dlls):
- Core.dll
- V8.dll

Comment 6 | author: ClearScriptLib | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/ClearFoundry/ClearScript/issues/364#issuecomment-1132924981
Hi again @arsi0001,
We were able to reproduce your issue by building for x64 and deploying to the HoloLens Emulator. Apparently the standard kernel32 library is unavailable on HoloLens, making it impossible to load native assemblies via [P/Invoke](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/native-interop/pinvoke). That turned out to be OK, as ClearScriptV8.win-x64.dll had been loaded automatically as a configured plugin.
Unfortunately, we then encountered another problem – the IL2CPP backend apparently supports Reverse P/Invoke but requires a non-standard attribute, `MonoPInvokeCallback`, to be applied to each entry point.
At this point we decided to abandon the effort. This HoloLens/Unity/IL2CPP platform seems to have incomplete compatibility with standard .NET runtimes, especially when it comes to dealing with unmanaged code.
Even if we could get it working, we'd have to provide special builds of the ClearScript managed assemblies – assuming the native ones work as is, which is unlikely – and publish them separately. Unfortunately, as ClearScript is a side project, supporting the major desktop platforms – including the eight CPU-specific V8 builds – is already stretching the limits of the resources available.
Have you considered using a pure .NET JavaScript engine such as [Jint](https://github.com/sebastienros/jint)?

<!-- source=github_issue; title=How to keep only one spawned object active when tracked image is detected; url=https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/arfoundation-samples/issues/663 -->

# How to keep only one spawned object active when tracked image is detected

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/arfoundation-samples/issues/663

I have this script where I instantiate an object on the tracked Image position, however, when I track the 2nd image after the 1st one, the GameObject associated with the first one doesn't become inactive.
```cs
[SerializeField]
private GameObject[] placeablePrefabs;
private Dictionary<string, GameObject> spawnedPrefabs = new Dictionary<string, GameObject>();
public ARTrackedImageManager trackedImageManager;
GameObject animalPrefab;
private void Awake()
{
foreach (GameObject prefab in placeablePrefabs)
{
GameObject newPrefab = Instantiate(prefab, Vector3.zero, Quaternion.identity);
newPrefab.name = prefab.name;
spawnedPrefabs.Add(prefab.name, newPrefab);
}
}
private void Update()
{
trackedImageManager.trackedImagesChanged += ImageChanged;
}
private void ImageChanged(ARTrackedImagesChangedEventArgs obj)
{
foreach (ARTrackedImage trackedImage in obj.added)
{
switch (trackedImage.referenceImage.name)
{
case "Dolphin":
Instantiate(placeablePrefabs[0], trackedImage.transform);
break;
case "Boa":
Instantiate(placeablePrefabs[1], trackedImage.transform);
break;
}
}
foreach (ARTrackedImage trackedImage in obj.updated)
{
//UpdateImage(trackedImage);
switch (trackedImage.referenceImage.name)
{
case "Dolphin":
animalPrefab = spawnedPrefabs["Dolphin"];
animalPrefab.transform.position = trackedImage.transform.position;
animalPrefab.SetActive(true);
break;
case "Boa":
animalPrefab = spawnedPrefabs["Boa"];
animalPrefab.transform.position = trackedImage.transform.position;
animalPrefab.SetActive(true);
break;
}
}
foreach (ARTrackedImage trackedImage in obj.removed)
{
spawnedPrefabs[trackedImage.referenceImage.name].SetActive(false);
}
}
```
I tried using this inside the foreach loop for obj.added and obj.removed
```cs
foreach (GameObject go in spawnedPrefabs.Values)
{
if (go.name != name)
{
go.SetActive(false);
}
}
```
However, this results in the app running super slow, almost unusable.
How can I make it so that any other GameObject besides the one that matches the tracked image name is disabled?
Any help is kindly appreciated
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: tdmowrer | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/arfoundation-samples/issues/663#issuecomment-726234421
I'm not sure I understand what you are trying to achieve. If both "Dolphin" and "Boa" are being tracked, then they will both be in the `updated` list.
If your goal is to only ever have one prefab active at a time, then I would put your `SetActive(false)` logic in the `added` loop -- this would deactivate all GameObjects except the most recently detected one.
Also, you should put this
```csharp
private void Update()
{
trackedImageManager.trackedImagesChanged += ImageChanged;
}
```
In an `OnEnable` or `Start` method. By doing this in `Update`, you are adding the same callback each frame, so `ImageChanged` will be called N times, where N is the number of frames your `MonoBehaviour` has been active.

You could try iterating over the dictionary's KeyValuePairs instead, since you have used the reference image name as the key:
```csharp
foreach (var kvp in spawnedPrefabs)
{
if (kvp.Key != name)
{
kvp.Value.SetActive(false);

```
