Comment 5 | author: tdmowrer | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/arfoundation-samples/issues/663#issuecomment-726991883
Hi Archer,
This issues page is really for questions about ARFoundation API usage. I can tell you how ARFoundation works, but I can't debug your code for you.
The [`trackedImagesChanged`](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.xr.arfoundation@4.0/api/UnityEngine.XR.ARFoundation.ARTrackedImageManager.html#UnityEngine_XR_ARFoundation_ARTrackedImageManager_trackedImagesChanged) event is triggered whenever any [reference image](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.xr.arsubsystems@4.0/manual/image-tracking.html#terminology) is
1. Newly detected (`added` list)
1. Updated (`updated` list)
1. Removed* (`removed` list)
If any of these occur during a frame, the event is triggered _once_ during that frame with the appropriate `added`, `updated`, and `removed` lists.
You only need to subscribe (e.g., `+= ImageChanged`) to the event once. It might be more appropriate to call this method `ImagesChanged` (plural) as it tells you about _all_ the added, updated, and removed images once per frame.
The specific result you are trying to achieve is possible, and I think you generally have the right approach, but you will need to debug it to find out why it is not working the way you expect. I suggest `Debug.Log`ing the names of the reference images as they are added/updated so that you can get an idea for what is happening. You can find that log output using [logcat](https://developer.android.com/studio/command-line/logcat) -- you can access it via the command line and filter for Unity-specific messages with
```adb logcat -s Unity```
Or you can use the [logcat package](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.mobile.android-logcat@latest) for a more integrated Unity experience.
\* Note that, since most AR frameworks can track moving images, they rarely consider images to be "removed" (i.e., cease to exist). Each tracked image also has a `trackingState` which is highly correlated with the device's ability to "see" it. See [these docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.xr.arfoundation@4.0/manual/tracked-image-manager.html#tracking-state) for details.

private void UpdatedImage(ARTrackedImage trackedImage)
{
switch (trackedImage.referenceImage.name)
{
case "Dolphin":
animalPrefab = spawnedPrefabs["Dolphin"];
animalPrefab.transform.position = trackedImage.transform.position;
animalPrefab.SetActive(true);
break;
case "Boa":
animalPrefab = spawnedPrefabs["Boa"];
animalPrefab.transform.position = trackedImage.transform.position;
animalPrefab.SetActive(true);
break;
}
foreach (Gameobject go in spawnedPrefabs.Values)
{
if (go.name != trackedImage.referenceImage.name)
{
go.SetActive(false);
}
}
}
```

Hi, I am a beginner for using unity. I met a problem when I tried to execute inputs. I searched for reasons but I still had no idea. The problems are shown in the picture.

Here is the part of codes:

Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: AlexRibard | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/barracuda-release/issues/72#issuecomment-657255977
Hi @JackWei0310
I've figured it out. We were missing a null_check in `ComputePrecompiled.Concat` causing the crash.
I've pushed a fix for the next version. I've also validated against ONNX runtime and get correct results.
In the meantime you can change your worker to be of type `Compute` it should work.
https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/barracuda-release/blob/release/1.0.0/Documentation%7E/Worker.md
Let me know
Comment 2 | author: AlexRibard | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/barracuda-release/issues/72#issuecomment-657256383
Regarding your comment,
We do some optimization under the hood, and the Relu gets fused in the Conv node, thus why you don't see the Relu node anymore.
You can toggle compile time optimization ON/OFF in the inspector:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12990800/87253431-27f13f80-c449-11ea-9899-7cc80211c212.png)
Comment 3 | author: AlexRibard | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/barracuda-release/issues/72#issuecomment-657593445
You can create it like this:
```
UnityEngine.Texture[] srcTextures = ...;
int channels = 3;
Tensor(srcTextures, channels, "myTensorName))
```
Comment 4 | author: JackWei0310 | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/barracuda-release/issues/72#issuecomment-657599351
> You can create it like this:
>
> ```
> UnityEngine.Texture[] srcTextures = ...;
> int channels = 3;
> Tensor(srcTextures, channels, "myTensorName))
> ```
I just quickly try it. The tensor will be (3,225,225,3), But actually I want (1,225,225,3). I want 3 textures can be merged as a channel.
Comment 5 | author: AlexRibard | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 9 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/barracuda-release/issues/72#issuecomment-657611869
Ah right, I see.
In that case, you'll need to create 3 individual tensors from your Textures and `Concat` them.
```
// build a new model that concats 3 inputs
var builder = new ModelBuilder();
builder.Concat("concat", new[] { "tensor0", "tensor1", tensor2" }, 3);
var worker = WorkerFactory.CreateWorker(builder.model, WorkerFactory.Device.GPU);
worker.Execute(new Dictionary<string, Tensor> { { "tensor0", tensor0 }, { "tensor1", tensor1 }, { "tensor2", tensor2 } });
Tensor tensor = worker.PeekOutput();
```
Comment 6 | author: AlexRibard | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 9 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/barracuda-release/issues/72#issuecomment-657635849
I would guess that the 3 input textures don't have the same spatial dimensions.
Be sure to resize them before creating the tensor.
the 3 tensors should have the same #batch #width #height for the Concat to work.
You can either resize by hand or by doing the following:
```
var targetRT0 = RenderTexture.GetTemporary(225, 225, 0);
Graphics.Blit(texture0, targetRT0, postprocessMaterial);
Tensor tensor0 = new Tensor(targetRT0, 1);
```

Comment 1 | author: DavidArayan | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 7 | url: https://github.com/DavidArayan/ezy-slice/issues/16#issuecomment-380674035
Greetings,
Thank you for the report. EzySlice should work wherever Unity can compile, since it's all written in C# with no external dependencies. I'll investigate this bug and get back to you.
Comment 2 | author: DavidArayan | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/DavidArayan/ezy-slice/issues/16#issuecomment-380674958
Greetings,
This is an interesting bug. Essentially it's saying that IntersectionResult is null which doesn't make sense because that instance shouldn't be deallocating for the duration of the slice. Have you by chance modified the source in any way? I'll continue digging.
Comment 3 | author: DavidArayan | association: OWNER | reactions: 2 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/DavidArayan/ezy-slice/issues/16#issuecomment-380676671
Greetings,
Thank you for the information. I'll continue digging. I have a suspicion that it may have something to do with the "ref" keyword, which is redundant considering IntersectionResult is a class. It's likely left over from when I changed IntersectionResult from a struct into a class. I'll write back once I've got a tested fix.
Comment 4 | author: DavidArayan | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 9 | url: https://github.com/DavidArayan/ezy-slice/issues/16#issuecomment-386957140
Greetings ymrg3307,
Apologies for the delay. I've sourced an Android device and will test and fix.
Comment 5 | author: DavidArayan | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/DavidArayan/ezy-slice/issues/16#issuecomment-386972417
Greetings ymrg3307,
I've tested on my end and didn't get any crashes. I did however fix a small issue on [master](https://github.com/DavidArayan/EzySlice/tree/master) branch. If you get the time, pull it down and try again. Other things to try are.
1) Switch between Il2CPP and Mono backends to see if it makes a difference
2) Check to make sure the android device is not running out of memory. I performed my test using a Samsung Galaxy s8 which is a high end device
3) Try out a new example in [Runtime Scene Example](https://github.com/DavidArayan/EzySlice-Example-Scenes/tree/master/EzySlice-Examples/Assets/Examples/Debug/Runtime) from the Example repository and see if you still get the crash.
Let me know how things go.
Comment 6 | author: DavidArayan | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/DavidArayan/ezy-slice/issues/16#issuecomment-388032902
Greetings ymrg3307,
Glad the problem got sorted! my Unity version defaults to the IL2CPP so I haven't actually tried mono myself. I know that mono is slowly being deprecated by the Unity team and IL2CPP is the way to go.
As for why it works, I'm not too sure. Hopefully someone with more experience with each backend can shed some light into the issue. The error from your logs actually occurs in a very odd place, the object that is causing the null reference cannot be null since the code never sets that object's reference to be null anywhere. I'm only doing guesstimates here so take this with a grain of salt..
1) Memory pressure actually forces Unity and/or Android to somehow deallocate the object prematurely at runtime, even though it shouldn't. This could be a bug in the mono backend?
2) The Garbage Collector prematurely deallocates the object, setting it to null which causes the rest of the code to crash. This should also never happen and if it does, then it's also a mono bug?
Other weird scenarios which "might" occur is that you are somehow destroying the Mono Script which is executing the slicing code, but I don't see how this can be done considering the whole thing is single threaded. Only way to do this would be outside of the main thread, and even then Unity shouldn't allow something like that to happen.
I'll keep this open for a while and see if someone with a bit more background on the Mono vs IL2CPP backends could provide a better answer!

I'm not super familiar with Unity. But maybe it has something to do with initialization not completing before the `Update()` method gets called continuously? Looks like `tracker` is the issue.
```csharp
// DebugRenderer.cs
private void OnEnable()
{
this.device = Device.Open(0);
var config = new DeviceConfiguration
{
ColorResolution = ColorResolution.r720p,
ColorFormat = ImageFormat.ColorBGRA32,
DepthMode = DepthMode.NFOV_Unbinned
};
device.StartCameras(config);
var calibration = device.GetCalibration(config.DepthMode, config.ColorResolution);
this.tracker = BodyTracker.Create(calibration);
debugObjects = new GameObject[(int)JointId.Count];
for (var i = 0; i < (int)JointId.Count; i++)
{
var cube = GameObject.CreatePrimitive(PrimitiveType.Cube);
cube.name = Enum.GetName(typeof(JointId), i);
cube.transform.localScale = Vector3.one * 0.4f;
debugObjects[i] = cube;
}
}
...
void Update()
{
using (Capture capture = device.GetCapture())
{
// FAILS HERE -- LINE 55
tracker.EnqueueCapture(capture);
var color = capture.Color;
if (color.WidthPixels > 0)
{
Texture2D tex = new Texture2D(color.WidthPixels, color.HeightPixels, TextureFormat.BGRA32, false);
tex.LoadRawTextureData(color.GetBufferCopy());
tex.Apply();
renderer.material.mainTexture = tex;
}
}
...
```
Comment 6 | author: thorikawa | association: MEMBER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/curiosity-inc/azure-kinect-dk-unity/issues/1#issuecomment-523746475
@ryanmjacobs Unity's console does not provide detailed info. Please see `~/Library/Logs/Unity/Editor.log` (if you run on the Editor) or `~/Library/Logs/DefaultCompany/azure-kinect-dk-unity/Player.log` (if you run the built app) assuming you use macOS. If you use other OSs, please see [here](https://docs.unity3d.com/2019.2/Documentation/Manual/LogFiles.html) for the log location. My guess is that either you did not put dlls and onnx file in the same folder as Assets or Cuda is not installed.

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/wave-harmonic/crest/issues/424

When I try to make a PS4 build I get these compile errors:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9056181/75015652-6b8ee100-5489-11ea-9ebb-761386561800.png)
Tested with built-in RP and Unity 2019.3.1f1 with a RTX 2060 Super on Win10.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: moosichu | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/wave-harmonic/crest/issues/424#issuecomment-589950945
Hi @woistjadefox looking at your post, you seem to have customised a few of the ocean shaders (I can see your shader is called `Crest/Ocean Modified` and that you have `OceanEmissionModified.hlsl` as well). Could you please try building the vanilla example project for PS4 and report the errors that you get there? At least we can track down the type-mismatch errors on our end - otherwise we have little to go-on in terms of which lines of code are causing the errors as we can't build for PS4 ourselves.

<!-- source=github_issue; title=Facebook SDK v7.16.0 NullReferenceExceptions on iOS; url=https://github.com/facebook/facebook-sdk-for-unity/issues/252 -->

# Facebook SDK v7.16.0 NullReferenceExceptions on iOS

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/facebook/facebook-sdk-for-unity/issues/252

After installing v7.16.0, the SDK throws an error almost every time I interact with it (for example when calling `FB.LogInWithReadPermissions`).
The error is as follows:
```
System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
at Facebook.Unity.CodelessUIInteractEvent.Update () [0x00000] in <00000000000000000000000000000000>:0
UnityEngine.DebugLogHandler:Internal_Log(LogType, String, Object)
UnityEngine.DebugLogHandler:LogFormat(LogType, Object, String, Object[])
UnityEngine.Logger:Log(LogType, Object)
UnityEngine.Debug:Log(Object)
Facebook.Unity.CodelessUIInteractEvent:Update()
(Filename: ./Runtime/Export/Debug.bindings.h Line: 45)
```
I'm using Unity 2018.4.0f1, Xcode 10.1, iOS 12.3.1 and .NET 4.x.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: timothymironenko-vgw | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 5 | url: https://github.com/facebook/facebook-sdk-for-unity/issues/252#issuecomment-500257912
I found this was happening when I upgraded to 7.16.0 from 7.15.1. I discovered that the issue seemed to related to the fact by upgrading and not doing a clean install of the SDK, some previous files were left over causing all sorts of conflicts. I suggest deleting the FacebookSDK folder and the PlayServicesResolver, and then reinstalling 7.16.0.
Comment 2 | author: myrik | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 6 | url: https://github.com/facebook/facebook-sdk-for-unity/issues/252#issuecomment-500543491
I'm having the same NullReferenceException on Android 9 using Unity 2018.3.10f1. I did try completely deleting the FacebookSDK folder before importing version 7.16.0
Comment 3 | author: num0n1 | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/facebook/facebook-sdk-for-unity/issues/252#issuecomment-502031534
same here, i did do a clean upgrade and still, on Unity 2018.3.1f1, target for android
`System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
at Facebook.Unity.CodelessUIInteractEvent.Update () [0x00096] in <9e96dd869f63450fb1f0ac2350bd157e>:0
UnityEngine.Debug:Log(Object)
Facebook.Unity.CodelessUIInteractEvent:Update()
`
Comment 4 | author: VoxelMatt | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 5 | url: https://github.com/facebook/facebook-sdk-for-unity/issues/252#issuecomment-508609945
I'm getting this issue in FB 7.17.0.
I've noticed that the Facebook SDK creates an EventSystem if one is not found, but my app manages it's own event systems. And if I delete the one that FB creates, then I get this error.
Can you just make the code try to find an existing event system if the one it has is deleted?
Thanks :)

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/realsenseai/librealsense/issues/2999

| Required Info | |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------- |
| Camera Model | D435 |
| Firmware Version | 05.10.13.00 |
| Operating System & Version | Win 10 |
| Platform | PC |
| SDK Version | current librealsense } |
| Language | C#/Unity } |

# Consider refactoring InputManager, MixedRealityCameraParent, Cursor to reduce dependencies

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1235

Currently scenes that have any of InputManager, MixedRealityCameraParent or a Cursor all have hard dependencies on the others.
If this is an absolute requirement, then the documentation should reflect this. Otherwise, this dependency chain along with Unity's uncertain load and unload order creates extra complexity around scene load and unload as well as enabling and disabling objects, or having scenes that might not require one of the components.
MixedRealityCameraParent without an InputManager throws:
```
NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.SetGlobalListener.OnEnable () (at
Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Utilities/SetGlobalListener.cs:16)
```
InputManager without a cursor throws:
```
Couldn't find cursor for "InputManager.SimpleSinglePointerSelector". UnityEngine.Debug:LogErrorFormat(Object, String, Object[])
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.SimpleSinglePointerSelector:FindCursorIfNeeded() (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Focus/SimpleSinglePointerSelector.cs:135)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.SimpleSinglePointerSelector:Start() (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Focus/SimpleSinglePointerSelector.cs:51)
```
DefaultCursor (I assume the other versions as well) without an InputManager throws:
```
NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.Cursor.RegisterManagers () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Cursor/Cursor.cs:183)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.Cursor.Start () (at assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Cursor/Cursor.cs:136)
```
```
NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.Cursor.UpdateCursorTransform () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Cursor/Cursor.cs:289)
HoloToolkit.Unity.InputModule.Cursor.Update () (at Assets/HoloToolkit/Input/Scripts/Cursor/Cursor.cs:143)
```
I'm not sure of all the interconnections and implications for how to refactor these, but for example, the MixedRealityCameraParent's SetGlobalListener OnEnable method requires an InputManager or it will throw a nullreference exception. Wrapping this in an if statement to check for null would remove the error but at the risk of the MixedRealityCameraParent never being added to the InputManager's GlobalListener if an InputManager is later added to the scene.
In this case, you could have the InputManager check for the existence of a MixedRealityCameraParent in the scene and then add it if it has not already been added to the GlobalListener array.

Comment 1 | author: jbienzms | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1235#issuecomment-347354757
Good catch @genereddick. I was actually coming here to open a ticket on **SetGlobalListener** using the value returned from **.Instance** without actually checking for an instance. This (and many of the others you've pointed out) are a continuing struggle with the [Singleton](MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/Assets/HoloToolkit/Utilities/Scripts/Singleton.cs) class.
The value returned by **Singleton.Instance** should _always_ be checked for null before using it, but unfortunately many classes in the toolkit still assume this property will not be null and start accessing the value using blindly. For example, **SetGlobalListener.cs** makes the following call without a check:
`InputManager.Instance.AddGlobalListener(gameObject);`
Instead, that line should probably be:
```
if (InputManager.Instance != null)
{
InputManager.Instance.AddGlobalListener(gameObject);
}
else
{
Debug.LogWarning("SetGlobalListener used but no InputManager found in the scene. This object will not be registered, even if an InputManager is added.");
}
```
Since this sort of check needs to happens a lot, we could look at adding a method to Singleton like this:
`Singleton.IfInstance(Action action, string message)`
And it could be called like this:
```
InputManager.IfInstance(()=>
{
InputManager.Instance.AddGlobalListener(gameObject);
}, "SetGlobalListener used but no InputManager found in the scene. This object will not be registered, even if an InputManager is added.");
```
The `message` parameter could also have a default value since we know the type of Singleton being searched for. In that case, `message` would be optional and only needed to give information about how the scene is affected without the service.
I don't know if this is a worthwhile pattern, especially based on how much code it saves. But it may serve as a reminder to not just access **.Instance** blindly.
Anyway, just a thought. Thanks again for catching these genereddick.

I believe the blind `Instance` use in early functions (`Awake`, `OnEnable`) is by-design, because of the above `Singleton` changes Stephen posted. If you're getting a null ref there, your scene isn't set up properly. Is there a scenario where `InputManager` won't exist in `Awake` but might later?
https://github.com/Microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1189#issuecomment-337378890
There's also [`IsInitialized`](https://github.com/Microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/blob/59726cdc3c0afccb8b8c3dc8d846a936e0ca1a3a/Assets/HoloToolkit/Utilities/Scripts/Singleton.cs#L57) that could be checked, but checking it in `Awake()` is incompatible with the singleton searching changes.
Comment 3 | author: jbienzms | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1235#issuecomment-347362808
> If you're getting a null ref there, your scene isn't set up properly.
I fully agree. The problem, as genereddick pointed out, is that there is no clue to the developer that the scene is setup incorrectly. For example, if you use the **MixedRealityCameraParent** prefab but don't ever add an **InputManager** to your scene you end up with a `NullReferenceException` instead of a helpful message informing you that an **InputManager** is required to use this prefab.
This is not the fault of the **MixedRealityCameraParent** prefab so much as it is the fault of the **SetGlobalListener** script that is part of that prefab. But again, the technical details of where the fault occurs aren't as important as the fact that the developer doesn't clearly know how to fix them.
> There's also IsInitialized that could be checked, but that check is incompatible with calling .Instance in the early functions before it gets set in its own Awake().
Could you elaborate on that a little? I'm reading that to mean that IsInitialized is valid sometimes but not always and I'd like to understand that better.
@keveleigh, any thoughts on how we can help this particular issue? Specifically, do you have any suggestions on how we could improve the scripts or the prefab so that if a user adds a **MixedRealityCameraParent** but forgets to add an **InputManager** the Unity log messages could guide them to do the right thing?
Comment 4 | author: keveleigh | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1235#issuecomment-347364155
If we change this to `objects.Length != 1`, that'll print out a message telling the user what was expected to exist but doesn't.
https://github.com/Microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/blob/59726cdc3c0afccb8b8c3dc8d846a936e0ca1a3a/Assets/HoloToolkit/Utilities/Scripts/Singleton.cs#L38
> Could you elaborate on that a little?
If `Instance` is called and the singleton exists in the scene but its `Awake` hasn't been called yet, the `Instance` call will search the scene and set itself. If `IsInitialized` is checked in a script's `Awake`, there's a chance `Instance` will be null (thus returning false) without the script searching the scene.
Comment 5 | author: keveleigh | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 2 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1235#issuecomment-347372796
> "MixedRealityCameraParent requires an InputManager in the scene but none was found."
is totally possible!
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3580640/33295912-47da1722-d38d-11e7-9868-ed69fe5f8a2b.png)
leads to
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3580640/33295926-5eaadd60-d38d-11e7-9a68-1628fda2a388.png)
My preference would be to find a way to do this in `Singleton`, though. This would be a very commonly reused bit of code, which is why we added the log in `Singleton` when more than one instance was found. I'm not sure the best way to get the GameObject name in there though.
Of course, if we're going through and refactoring anyway, like this Issue asks, perhaps it wouldn't be too bad to follow this pattern everywhere.
Comment 6 | author: jbienzms | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 2 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/1235#issuecomment-347580684
> is totally possible!
This looks perfect! But my question is, where did the `name` field come from that is used in your `Debug.LogError` message? And how did it get set to the string `"MixedRealityCameraParent"`?
> Wish there was a way to know who called it.
Precisely. That would be ideal. But without doing a stack walk I don't think that's possible. Especially with a property. One of the reasons I was suggesting the **IfInstance** method above was to provide more information about the caller or the request. But again that might be overkill.
I believe @keveleigh may be proposing we add a `name` (or `requester`?) field to **SetGlobalListner**? If so that could help with the prefab issue because that field could be set as part of the **MixedRealityCameraParent** prefab. But that doesn't help with the other two mentioned in this issue and I agree it would be much nicer to solve this in **Singleton** itself. I just don't see a way to solve it through the **.Instance** property alone.
It may be worth discussing at this point that what we're really trying to solve for with the Singleton class is effectively Inversion of Control (or IoC). And here's a great MSDN Article that compares [IoC Containers and Singletons](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/magazine/jj991965.aspx).
It's probably overkill, but one possible solution would be to actually use an IoC Container. If we did, the **Singleton** base class would simply call `Container.Register` when it's activated. As with other IoC systems, the Container would then be responsible for making sure there is only once instance (or named instance, etc.)
Even if we didn't opt for a full IoC container, we could still opt for using some of the patterns. For example, instead of a **.Instance** _property_ we could opt for a **.GetInstance** _method_. This would allow **.GetInstance** to thrown an exception when the service is missing, and another method **.GetInstanceOrDefault** would work like the **.Instance** property does today. If these were methods instead of properties, we could also have optional string parameter(s) that describe the caller and / or use case. That information could then be propagated into any log or exception messages.
Anyway, just thinking out loud here again.

<!-- source=github_issue; title=[vNext] Proposed Fixes for Singleton; url=https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/486 -->

# [vNext] Proposed Fixes for Singleton

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/486

I know this may be an unpopular topic, but personally I feel it's time we discuss the implementation of Singleton in the toolkit.
For those who aren't aware, many classes in the toolkit inherit from [Singleton](https://github.com/Microsoft/HoloToolkit-Unity/blob/d343a0897f43ba0094d8e5ca032dc3a243cf2712/Assets/HoloToolkit/Utilities/Scripts/Singleton.cs). In programming, Singleton is a pattern used to “ensure that only one instance of the singleton class ever exists” (that’s from [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singleton_pattern)). But the **Singleton** class in HoloToolkit doesn't guarantee only a single instance exists. In fact, it doesn't guarantee that any instance exists at all. What **Singleton** in the toolkit does is _return the last instance to become Awake in the Unity scene hierarchy_.
Here are some problems that commonly occur with the current implementation:
1. If no instance of the behavior is placed anywhere in the scene, **Singleton.Instance** will return **null**. No exception is thrown and no error will be presented in the log window.
2. If more than one instance of the behavior is placed in the scene, there is no guarantee which instance will actually be returned by **Singleton.Instance**. This is because the internal instance is set on [Awake](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.Awake.html?_ga=1.89456667.1248899417.1470239847) and the order in which Awake is called is random. With the current design of **Singleton.Instance**, the last one Awake wins.
3. Many behaviors currently use the object returned by **Singleton.Instance** without checking first to see if it's **null**. If the user has forgotten to place the behavior in the scene, this results in a non-descriptive **NullReferenceException** at runtime and the calling **GameObject** is disabled. This is challenging to debug and very confusing for new Unity developers.
There are currently **271** uses of **.Instance** in the HoloToolkit. Of those 271, only a tiny fraction (maybe 10 or so) actually check to see if the instance is valid before using it. This opens up a very large possibility of error, and when one does occur it's difficult to solve.
I propose the following changes:
1. **Singleton** should be renamed **SceneInstance**
2. The **.Instance** property should be renamed **.First**
3. The **.First** property will log a descriptive error _and throw a descriptive exception_ if no instance is available. Something like "An instance of " + typeof(T).Name + " could not be found in the scene."
4. A new **.FirstOrDefault** property will be added which does not throw an exception. This is for cases where it's OK that a behavior may not exist in the scene.
5. A log message will be generated _and exception thrown_ if more than one instance of the same behavior is added to the scene.
The **.First** and **.FirstOrDefault** names as well as their proposed implementation both follow the conventions used in System.Linq for [IEnumerable](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/system.linq.enumerable_methods(v=vs.110).aspx).
These proposed changes correct the misuse of 'Singleton', follow a known pattern, and properly notify the user if they accidentally leave a required behavior out of a scene.
I'm open to thoughts and feedback. I'm also willing to implement these changes if others agree they would be beneficial.
Selected solution comments:

Comment 4 | author: shilohjames | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/486#issuecomment-386541458
Reading through the above discussion, I see some interesting points raised which allude to use cases I may not be familiar with. That said, it seems apparent that we're actually covering two related but distinct concepts which ultimately should be split into two separate discussions:
**1) *Singleton* pattern objects:** Objects which should have no more than one instance instantiated at any one time across all currently loaded Scenes, and which should be accessible from any Scene. These may or may not be made persistent instances, depending upon the particular use case they are intended to fulfil.
**2) *Scene-Singleton* pattern objects:** Objects which should have no more than one instance instantiated within any one Scene, but which may have additional instances which each exist in other Scenes, and which may or may not be accessible from other Scenes.
Personally I have not encountered a use case for a *SceneSingleton* pattern in Unity, primarily because the *Singleton* pattern performs almost the same function when used in conjunction with Unity's *SceneManagement* feature set, for every use case I have personally encountered in production environments. While I *can* envision a few use cases for this pattern, I also find myself wondering whether there is need for this feature within the MRTK, and invite further discussion from other participants on this point.
The main concern I see with the current implementation of *SingleInstance* is that it presents itself as being of a Singleton pattern, but is in actuality an implementation of the *SceneSingleton* pattern exhibiting modified behaviour that is inconsistent with the standard Singleton pattern, and which is also inconsistent with Unity's recommended MonoBehaviour logic flow, for the following reasons:
---
**a) *SingleInstance* uses lazy instance referencing relying upon `Object.FindObjectsOfType<T>()` to acquire its first instance *from the currently active Scene*.** This is a flawed approach as it i) does not support finding instances within additively loaded Scenes unless the hosting Scene has previously been marked as active within Unity's *SceneManager* (See link below for reference), ii) does not warn the user if other instances exist within Scenes which are currently loaded but are not the currently active Scene, and iii) even with these restrictions has a performance described as 'very slow' by *Unity Technologies* as internally it requires a `GameObject.GetComponent<T>()` search on every GameObject within a full Scene hierarchy traversal.
It is possible to address this issue by having the component iterate through all currently loaded Scenes to find all instances, however this is an even less performant solution than the current implementation, and I am aware of no more performant approach that does not require an unnecessarily complicated solution.
> Unity Documentation, Script reference: `Object.FindObjectsOfType<T>`
> https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Object.FindObjectsOfType.html
**Proposed fix:** Singleton instance references should be checked and set explicitly by the valid instance, using its `this` property.
---
**b) *SingleInstance* does not follow Unity's recommended logic flow.** The recommended logic flow of MonoBehaviour-derived objects is to initialise themselves within their `Awake()` method (See link below for reference), within which they do not attempt to access any instances of other Components which cannot be guaranteed to exist at that time. This is when the reference to the Singleton instance should be set. If a MonoBehaviour does need to access other Components which are saved to (and thus, initialised within the same frame as other Components in) the currently loading Scene, they should do so *no earlier than* within their `OnEnable()`, or ideally within their `Start()` methods.
> Unity Documentation, MonoBehaviour Event Execution Order:
> https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/ExecutionOrder.html
**Proposed fix:** Singleton reference should be set in the Component's `Awake()` method, and derived components should not access other Components until `OnEnable()` or `Start()` methods are executed.
---
**c) *SingleInstance* attempts to address issues in other MRTK components.** Implementing the two fixes proposed above exposes several cases of other components exhibiting the behaviour described in point b) above, in which they attempt to naively access one or more *SingleInstance* components which are either uninitialised or non-existent at time of execution. These issues may or may not be encountered in any individual project, depending upon feature inclusion, hierarchy layout, and loading order of Scenes containing derived components.
Referring to the class summary of the current implementation of *SingleInstance*, it seems clear that it was intended to address these issues, however it does so inadequately, and also introduces some serious and untenable issues of its own.
**Proposed fix:** Other components should be refactored as necessary to make their behaviour consistent with the recommended flow of *MonoBehaviour* components.
---
**d) No support currently exists for raising an event once the Singleton instance has been initialised.** In past and current projects, I have found it useful to be able to have external Components subscribe to an event which will be fired once a particular Singleton has successfully initialised.
One notable example from the MRTK is the *WorldAnchorManager*'s asynchronous loading of the stored *WorldAnchor* collection, the completion of which is in effect a prerequisite to the *WorldAnchorManager* being *completely* initialised. The reason for this process being asynchronous is apparent, however the constraint does require that other Components are able to safely track when that initialisation has taken place, and the cleanest way to do this is to allow those Components to subscribe to an OnInitialisationComplete event defined within the *WorldAnchorManager*. For similar reasons other *Singleton*s may benefit from this functionality, even if is used only to allow them to announce that they now exist and may be accessed, and it seems worthwhile to implement this in the base class.
**Proposed fix:** Add a method with the signature `public static void RaiseOnInitialisedOrNow(Action callback)`, which raises the injected callback immediately if the instance has been initialised at time of execution, or stores it for later execution within the *Singleton*'s `Awake()` method once initialisation has completed successfully.
---
**e) With the above changes, the class should be renamed appropriately.** This is more of a code clarity concern, and is predicated upon the assumption that the intent of any entity should be apparent and clear from its name alone. Currently this intent is not served by the name of the *SingleInstance* class.
**Proposed fix:** The class is a generic extension of *MonoBehaviour* which implements *Singleton* functionality, so I propose the name `MonoBehaviourSingleton<T>` as an alternative.
---
**f) The above changes do not provide support for SceneSingleton functionality.** If deemed necessary, to cover the use case of having multiple instances of a component which implements singleton-like functionality, but with the specific constraint of having no more than one instance in any single *Scene*, and which may allow cross-Scene instance access, another component should be created to provide this functionality.
**Proposed fix:** Another thread should be created with this topic as its subject matter.
---
**Contraindications:**
While the proposed code changes to this class are relatively trivial, from making similar changes to our local (older) copy of the MRTK it has become clear that the effect upon dependant classes is not. In particular, it will expose a number of issues related to the behaviour described above in point c) throughout the MRTK, each of which will likely need to be addressed as separate issues. With that in mind, it is best that this proposal be considered for a later version which includes further modifications to other MRTK components.
Comment 5 | author: SimonDarksideJ | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 6 | score: 11 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/486#issuecomment-387459430
Seconded, a fantastic writeup @shilohjames :D
As @StephenHodgson points out, we are leaving Singleton out of the picture as much as possible, to the extent that there will only be ONE singleton in the MRTK (core).
Instead, we are using a managed container approach approach where all "entities" in the MRTK will subscribe and be managed by the Mixed Reality manager. This will also be extensible enough to support both MRTK components and runtime client components. This also reduces our dependancy on MonoBehaviour to the same extent.
This addresses a lot of what you have described:
* 1) Singleton pattern objects:
MRTK Managers are single instance in the running project, with Little to no MonoBehaviour impact (which makes them over 30% faster)
* 2) Scene-Singleton pattern objects
The MRTK manager has a separate container for "run-time" components, utilising the same logic. And more importantly, utilising the same API
* a) SingleInstance uses lazy instance referencing
Completely gone, the Container approach means you have a single place for finding a manager using a discovery pattern which is very fast. No searching of scene as we effectively don't use it.
* b) SingleInstance does not follow Unity's recommended logic flow.
Again, decoupled from MonoBehaviour, so we control the logic flow.
But from your feedback, you have covered somethings which I have not yet accounted for, namely:
* d) No support currently exists for raising an event once the Singleton instance has been initialised.
We do have events throughout the new system, in fact it is mostly event driven. However, the Manager itself doesn't currently raise events for new / existing components.
**Will add this**
* f) The above changes do not provide support for SceneSingleton functionality.
Although runtime components in the manager are managed separately and can be flushed, this was designed around run-time, not necessarily scene switching.
**Will review and look at Scene Flushing / reuse**
Keep an eye on the vNext branch (and the MixedRealityManager) to see more of what's coming. As soon as It's demo'able, no doubt Stephen and I will take to the stage 🗡
Comment 6 | author: StephenHodgson | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 6 | score: 8 | url: https://github.com/microsoft/MixedRealityToolkit-Unity/issues/486#issuecomment-433777295
See my blog post on medium explaining how we solved this problem in vNEXT.
https://medium.com/@stephen_hodgson/the-mixed-reality-framework-6fdb5c11feb2

I think that this change is affected.
https://unity3d.com/jp/unity/whats-new/unity-2017.2.0
> Backwards Compatibility Breaking Changes
> * Scripting: UnityEngine.dll is now split into separate dlls for each UnityEngine module.
So, it seems to be solved in this way.
http://answers.unity3d.com/questions/206665/typegettypestring-does-not-work-in-unity.html
```diff
diff --git a/src/UnityExtension/Assets/Editor/GitHub.Unity/Misc/Utility.cs b/src/UnityExtension/Assets/Editor/GitHub.Unity/Misc/Utility.cs
index e645e565..0deb4c97 100644
--- a/src/UnityExtension/Assets/Editor/GitHub.Unity/Misc/Utility.cs
+++ b/src/UnityExtension/Assets/Editor/GitHub.Unity/Misc/Utility.cs
@@ -32,7 +32,7 @@ namespace GitHub.Unity
static StreamExtensions()
{
- var t = typeof(Texture2D).Assembly.GetType("UnityEngine.ImageConversion", false, false);
+ var t = Assembly.Load("UnityEngine.dll").GetType("UnityEngine.ImageConversion", false, false);
if (t != null)
{
// looking for ImageConversion.LoadImage(this Texture2D tex, byte[] data)
```
Comment 5 | author: shana | association: MEMBER | reactions: 2 | score: 17 | url: https://github.com/github-for-unity/Unity/issues/351#issuecomment-339096706
*shakes fist at Unity*
Ok so the problem is that `ImageConversion` got moved out to a separate DLL, which means using `Texture2D` as a DLL location base no longer works. Worse, it got moved to its own assembly - literally a DLL which only contains this class, which means there is no type we can use to get at its location. So, sigh, we'll need to add yet another codepath to the `StreamExtensions` code to reference the `UnityEngine.ImageConversionModule.dll` dll and get the `ImageConversion` type.
Comment 6 | author: joegoldin | association: NONE | reactions: 6 | score: 8 | url: https://github.com/github-for-unity/Unity/issues/351#issuecomment-339771003

<!-- source=github_issue; title=Can I open and edit the scenes from procthor-10k dataset in Unity.editor?; url=https://github.com/allenai/ai2thor/issues/1128 -->

# Can I open and edit the scenes from procthor-10k dataset in Unity.editor?

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/allenai/ai2thor/issues/1128

Now I can edit the scenes in ai2thor in Unity.editor, but I don't know how to edit scenes in procthor-10k dataset in Unity.editor.
I guess the root of the problem is that how to build a unity scene file from a scene.json
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: winthos | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 2 | score: 17 | url: https://github.com/allenai/ai2thor/issues/1128#issuecomment-1470789780
So the challenge of editing a procthor scene in-editor is that all procthor scenes are generated at runtime, so they are not saved or cached in a way that you can open up a usual Unity scene.
The best way to "open" a procthor scene in the editor is to take the json and place it in the directory `Assets/Resources/rooms`
Then, go to `Assets/Scenes/Procedural` and open up the `Procedural.unity` scene.
While in this scene, hit `Play` and then navigate your cursor to the text box that shows up to the bottom left of the `Game` window that reads "Enter text..."
This box allows actions to be executed directly in the editor without needing to link to the python controller, and all actions are defined in the script `DebugInputField.cs` located in `Assets/Scripts`
To start, type `initp` into this box to initialize a default agent and press `enter` to execute. Then, type `chp <json file's name>` and hit `enter` again to generate a house based on the json file you saved to the `Assets/Resources/rooms` directory.
From here, you will be able to see and manipulate the objects created based on the json, however editing them here will not save the json. You will need to then go back into the json and edit any new values like changed object positions, by taking the values of manipulated objects in the editor and copying them over into the json itself.

Comment 4 | author: winthos | association: COLLABORATOR | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/allenai/ai2thor/issues/1128#issuecomment-1511838496
> Thank you! I open the procthor scene in unity.editor successfully ，now,I want to save the scene as an Asset file,how to make it? @winthos
The `ProcTHOR` scenes are all generated dynamically at runtime based on the parameters specified in the json for each scene. Because of this, there is no way to save a scene in the traditional sense as a Unity scene file as the scene itself only exists at runtime. Any changes you want to make in the Unity Editor you will need to log and then make those same updates to the json for that scene in order to "save" your changes.

<!-- source=github_issue; title=SteamVR_Actions broken after Scene reload; url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steamvr_unity_plugin/issues/616 -->

# SteamVR_Actions broken after Scene reload

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steamvr_unity_plugin/issues/616

If you use the SteamVR interaction system in Unity and setup default parameters via
`SteamVR_Action_Boolean someAction = SteamVR_Input.GetAction<SteamVR_Action_Boolean>("InteractUI");`
the interaction system gets broken if you change the button type in the inspector to something other than the default value and then reload the scene in play mode. The problem persists until you restart Unity.
Use this script to see yourself:
```
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.SceneManagement;
using Valve.VR;
public class InteractionBug : MonoBehaviour
{
public SteamVR_Action_Boolean button = SteamVR_Input.GetAction<SteamVR_Action_Boolean>("InteractUI");
void Update()
{
if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Space))
SceneManager.LoadScene(SceneManager.GetActiveScene().name);
}
}
```
To Reproduce:
1. Open a new Unity Project
2. Import Steam VR
3. Generate the default SteamVR Inputs
4. Create a new Scene
5. Delete the Main Camera
6. Pull in the Player Prefab ( from SteamVR/InteractionSystem/Core/Prefabs )
7. Add the provided Script to any GameObject in the scene
8. Go to that GameObject and change the Button in the Inspector to something else as InteractUI
9. Press play and observe any of the Hand scrips from the Player in scene
10. Now press space to reload the scene
11. Observe the Player Hands again and note that the Ui Interact Action has changed to whatever you selected in the provided script to at step 8
12. The Ui Interact Action is now broken and can't be changed reversed to the original button and Unity must be restarted in order to do so
Or download this project I set up and just try it out (you can skip step 1 - 8 then)
https://github.com/Noblauch/SteamVR_Interaction_Bug
**Expected:**
The SteamVR_Input.GetAction<SteamVR_Action_Boolean>("InteractUI") function only gets the defined (bound) button for the specific action and doesn't have the ability to actually change or destroy something.
It took me 2 days and overall ~19 hours at work to even figure out what the hell is going on. I really hope this gets fixed and some poor soul finds this post, so he doesn't need to commit -m "suicide"
My question now would still be how to initialize a button for the inspector because this way is breaking the system. However it's actually exactly done like that in the interaction system example scene.

OK, so after fighting with this for 2 days, I think I have resolved my issues with the following:
First, I reverted to a single action set and removed default values in MonoBehaviours for action sets as @Noblauch mentioned, e.g., `public SteamVR_ActionSet actionSet = SteamVR_Input.GetActionSet("default");` => `public SteamVR_ActionSet actionSet;` . This appeared to fix the issue!
Next I added my other action sets back in and my hands stopped tracking again after the SECOND scene load (Menu => Game => Menu*), however, the default action set didn't disappear from Unity anymore, so, progress.
After more experimentation I found that if I *disabled all action sets* before loading new scenes then the hands would work after loading. Maybe enabling a previously active action set just doesn't work after scene switching?
If this is the expected way to use action sets, it would be nice if disabling all action sets was done by `SteamVR_LoadLevel` automatically.

# Problems when adding a labeler to a perception camera

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.perception/issues/578

Hi! I'm using the Perception package in a URP project, so I'm using the 0.11 version.
I want to label objects spawned by users at runtime and refer to the suggestions in #467. When there are no objects spawned dynamically, I can create a perception camera and add a labeler to it. However, after destroying the old perception camera and creating a new perception camera in order to label newly generated objects, I fail to attach a labeler to it. My code looks like
```
var followCameraObject = GameObject.FindGameObjectWithTag("camBase");
if (followCameraObject.GetComponent<PerceptionCamera>() != null) {
Destroy(followCameraObject.GetComponent<PerceptionCamera>());
}
followCameraObject.AddComponent<PerceptionCamera>();
followCameraObject.GetComponent<PerceptionCamera>().AddLabeler(semanticSegmentationLabeler);
```
I also tried not to destroy the perception camera but to remove the labeler, but I got NullReferenceException when I use code like
```
var followCameraObject = GameObject.FindGameObjectWithTag("camBase");
followCameraObject.GetComponent<PerceptionCamera>().RemoveLabeler(followCameraObject.GetComponent<PerceptionCamera>().m_lablers[0]);
```
Would you like to give me some advice on how to label the runtime-spawned objects via script?
Appreciate your help!
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: mark1ng123 | association: NONE | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/com.unity.perception/issues/578#issuecomment-1457910392
Hey it is really hard to follow your code, can you edit the issue and fix the code identation please.
I did attach daynamiclly the lablers the steps are:
1. Get the componenet for the perception camera, `Camera=GameObject.Find("MainCamera").GetComponent<PerceptionCamera>();`
2. Create a labling config object,
` var Config = ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<UnityEngine.Perception.GroundTruth.LabelManagement.IdLabelConfig>();
`
3. Add a labeling counter if you have many labels, ` int labelCounter = 1 `
4. Then attach them to a label management list,
```
List<UnityEngine.Perception.GroundTruth.LabelManagement.IdLabelEntry> labels;
foreach (string label in labels)
{
labels.Add(new UnityEngine.Perception.GroundTruth.LabelManagement.IdLabelEntry{id = labelCounter, label = label});
labelCounter++;
}
```
5. intialize the config with the list you created: `Config.Init(entries); `
6. Then add the corect labler in your case is semantic segmentation so :
` Camera.AddLabeler(new UnityEngine.Perception.GroundTruth.Labelers.SemanticSegmentationLabeler(Config));
`
And thats it you have a labler set and ready to run.
Note: dont forget to add the right lables to the gameobjects, you can also do it during runtime, i also recommend it to give a more dynamic feel

You are successfully logged in when you see the log message:
```
Connected to arenaxr.org:8883...
```
If the error `TaskCanceledException: A task was canceled.` occurs after that point, your account is totally fine, but it's likely something has prematurely terminated your unity application or network connection. It's harder to replicate, but we can try and simulate some scenarios.

Comment 3 | author: mwfarb | association: CONTRIBUTOR | reactions: 0 | score: 8 | url: https://github.com/arenaxr/arena-unity/issues/131#issuecomment-2815958746
I'm glad you got though the auth flow!
I can confirm the original `TaskCanceledException` during the browser auth flow is likely from a timeout. I can simulate the same error by forcing the auth flow timeout to a few seconds. I can improve the error messaging there.
Is it possible you have a computer firewall or network firewall that is limiting connections, particularly on `localhost`? That original flow will typically run a temporary server on your machine using a random port like `http://127.0.0.1:49343` which will try and reach out to `google.com` looking for the completed state of you selecting and confirming the account to use. If something is blocking your machine from making those connections it will timeout.
Standby for a release to improve those error messages.

# NullReferenceException Error

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/aras-p/UnityGaussianSplatting/issues/153

Hi, I use Unity 6 with the Universal Render Pipeline (URP). I want to import the GSfile into my VR project. I unzipped the UnityGaussianSplatting-main folder and only copied the entire PACKAGE folder into my project path under ASSETS/GAUSSIANSPLAT.
The creation of the GaussianSplatAsset works, but when I try to add the Data Asset, I encounter the following errors:
NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
GaussianSplatting.Runtime.GaussianSplatRenderer.InitSortBuffers (System.Int32 count) (at Assets/UnityGaussianSplatting/Runtime/GaussianSplatRenderer.cs:428)
GaussianSplatting.Runtime.GaussianSplatRenderer.CreateResourcesForAsset () (at Assets/UnityGaussianSplatting/Runtime/GaussianSplatRenderer.cs:407)
GaussianSplatting.Runtime.GaussianSplatRenderer.Update () (at Assets/UnityGaussianSplatting/Runtime/GaussianSplatRenderer.cs:612)
I apologize for my questions, but I would be really appreciate if you can help me:
1. Is there a way to import UnityGaussianSplatting as a Unity Package to use in my own project?
2. Based on the error above, could it be due to missing files that I didn’t copy into the correct path?
3. I haven’t tried single or multi-pass rendering yet; is single-pass supported?
Thank you!

> Execute is not implemented; the pass GaussianSplatting.Runtime.GaussianSplatURPFeature+GSRenderPass won't be executed in the current render loop. UnityEngine.GUIUtility:ProcessEvent (int, intptr, bool&)
> I hope this configuration will be suitable for VR developers. What are your thoughts?

# Host/client desync

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/tesinormed/FAndCDaveCo/issues/1

Howdy! Been noticing an issue while using this mod with my friends where when someone died, the "Days Left Until Quota" desynced for us when everyone was revived, and the ship lever was stuck in the "Wait until ship has landed" position. I did some testing with 1 friend and the resulting error only showed on client side, not host side. Something also of note was that I saw the deductions made when people died, but my friends did not.
`[Error : Unity Log] NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
Stack trace:
tesinormed.FAndCDaveCo.Network.State.get_DisableDeathCreditPenalty () (at ./Network/State.cs:16)
(wrapper dynamic-method) StartOfRound+<EndOfGame>d__278.DMD<StartOfRound+<EndOfGame>d__278::MoveNext>(StartOfRound/<EndOfGame>d__278)
tesinormed.FAndCDaveCo.Patches.StartOfRound_EndOfGame_Patch+<Postfix>d__2.MoveNext () (at ./Patches/StartOfRound_EndOfGame_Patch.cs:114)
UnityEngine.SetupCoroutine.InvokeMoveNext (System.Collections.IEnumerator enumerator, System.IntPtr returnValueAddress) (at <e27997765c1848b09d8073e5d642717a>:0)`
Some notes
- During all of these issues, we did not use any of the terminal commands associated with this mod
- This error occurred with both 1 person dying or a whole team wipe
- This issue was replicated with only F&C Dave Co (and dependencies)
Hope this helps! When this mod works, it saves runs. 😄 Thanks much for it!

> I'm going to close this for now as we don't have enough information to go on. Please feel free to reopen when you can reproduce it.
Hello, I finally understood the problem. The problem was something different than I thought.
During recording on Android (maybe also on iOS too)
- Press home button or switch to another app
- Foreground the game
- My game has pause menu so they either click restart or home button
- The Recorder component gets destroyed so which also crashes the game

#### Couple of questions:
- How should I structure my code when user puts the game in background?
a. Should I expect the recorder continue to work when they puts the game in foreground?
b. Should I stop the recorder immediately when the game is put in background?
- Where should I put the recorder game object?
a. A global `GameObject` with `DontDestroyOnLoad` so it never gets destroyed unexpectedly?
b. A local `GameObject` but it should stop the recording immediately when it gets destroyed?
- Do you know what happens when user receives a notification and user peeks it by sliding down from top. I guess it's also considered as `background`?

# Can't respawn with mod enabled.

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/Shaosil/LethalCompanyMods-GeneralImprovements/issues/101

My friends and I were playing and we downloaded this mod. I'm not sure if it's due to another mod conflicting with this one or not but the problem is that after the ship takes off people don't respawn, and instead the game is softlocked on the ship where no one can respawn. Comment 5 | author: Shaosil | association: OWNER | reactions: 2 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/Shaosil/LethalCompanyMods-GeneralImprovements/issues/101#issuecomment-1922522091
Well it always seems to be happening with the toggle monitor power function. I'm working on adding some more foolproof null checks to that, hopefully this will all be fixed in the next version.
Edit: I guess to add some technical detail for what I think is happening: during StartOfRound.Start(), I'm calling a function that makes whatever monitor changes are necessary based on the config. Part of that function handles storing some variables. To fix this, I'm going to store one of the references I need later (in ToggleMonitorPower) AND check if each variable is null before each use. These particular variables are just instances of the vanilla profit quota and deadline canvas objects, which I believe Corporate Restructure is plain deleting (making it VERY incompatible with mods that reference those). However, if I copy the references before that happens and combine that with the null checks, the objects either won't be around to care about, or they will and I'll still see them.
TL:DR; I'll fix it by not using the objects that are being deleted unexpectedly :)

# gRPC + IL2CPP for Unity fails to build

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/22485

### What version of gRPC and what language are you using?
C# on Unity with IL2CPP, Tried with both gRPC for Unity 2.29 and 2.26.
### What operating system (Linux, Windows,...) and version?
Windows 10
### What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g. python version or version of gcc)
IL2CPP with .NET 4.0 compatibility, version 2019.3.6f1.
### What did you do?
1. Create new project with the above setup.
2. Set the project type to IL2CPP.
3. Unzip the gRPC zip into the Assets folder.
4. Add any C# script that uses the gRPC library, and attach it to a cube or any GameObject (This was the one I've used)
```cs
public class TestScript : MonoBehaviour
{
// Start is called before the first frame update
void Start()
{
var client = new CerisCore.CerisCoreClient(new Channel("grpc.project-ceris.com", 443, new SslCredentials()));
var r = client.GetStatic(new Empty());
Debug.Log(r);
}
}
```
5. Run it, which works correctly in editor (IIRC, which runs with Mono, even when you set build to IL2CPP)
6. Build Project (for Windows)
### What did you expect to see?
Builds and runs successfully.
### What did you see instead?
Runs successfully in editor (as mentioned above, IIRC uses Mono even with IL2CPP builds), but when building w/ IL2CPP, crashes with this logging:

Comment 2 | author: TheCactusBlue | association: NONE | reactions: 4 | score: 14 | url: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/22485#issuecomment-604502885
Ok, I came up with a really hacky solution, that (kinda) worked.
1. Download both the gRPC source repository and the unity package.
2. Unzip the unity package into `/Plugins`.
3. Delete the contents of the `Grpc.Core`, and `Grpc.Core.Api`, excluding `runtimes`.
4. Copy in the source for the `Grpc.Core`, and `Grpc.Core.Api`.
5. Add the three functions from above into the dummy.
6. Comment out the methods, annotations, and classes that cause error, from AssemblyInfo, ForwardedTypes, and UnimplementedCallInvoker.
7. Comment out the DefaultSslOverride.
8. Modify NativeMethods in NativeExtension.cs:
```cs
private static NativeMethods LoadNativeMethodsUnity()
{
// GetUnityRuntimePlatform causes error
return new NativeMethods(new NativeMethods.DllImportsFromSharedLib());
//switch (PlatformApis.GetUnityRuntimePlatform())
//{
// case "IPhonePlayer":
// return new NativeMethods(new NativeMethods.DllImportsFromStaticLib());
// default:
// // most other platforms load unity plugins as a shared library
// return new NativeMethods(new NativeMethods.DllImportsFromSharedLib());
//}
}
```
9. Copy the certs from the `/etc/roots.pem` into the Assets/Resource folder.
10. When creating the channel, feed the certificate manually, with:
```cs
new Channel("grpc.project-ceris.com", 443, new SslCredentials(Resources.Load<TextAsset>("roots").text));
```
11. For some reason, when you try to exit the game in IL2CPP build, the game crashes (and exits anyways). A workaround I've found is to call
```cs
chan.ShutdownAsync().Wait();
```
when you exit Unity.
I'm still keeping this issue open, for these minor bugs.

<!-- source=github_issue; title=Relative Volume Path 를 이용하여 Dicom Image Viewer 를 구현하기; url=https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9 -->

# Relative Volume Path 를 이용하여 Dicom Image Viewer 를 구현하기

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9

### 요구사항
- Dicom Study 의 Relative Volume Path 를 이용하여 Dicom Volume 을 캐시로 다운로드
- Volume 이 있으면 그 Volume 을 사용하고 없으면 웹에서 다운로드
- Normalized 된 배열을 이용해 Texture 를 만들고 화면에 출력
- Slider 로 이미지 Index 를 바꿔가면서 Image 를 볼 수 있도록 구현
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: hsskia | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9#issuecomment-2024402729
### 해결 과정 1
- 기존에 text 형식으로 되어있는 Series Data 를 button 형식으로 바꿈
![image](https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/assets/162946806/9ce313d9-f394-40c9-ae0c-4a67935daac9)
- Series Data 를 클릭하면 해당 Data 와 일치하는 Nrrd 파일을 다운로드 받도록함
- `File.Exists()` 함수를 통해 Nrrd 파일이 이미 폴더에 존재하면 다시 웹에서 다운로드 받지 않도록
Comment 2 | author: hsskia | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9#issuecomment-2024700834
### 해결 과정 2
- `Application.persistentDataPath` 를 통해 unity 파일 경로에 nrrd 파일 저장
- slider 를 움직이면 slider index 에 일치하는 value 가 출력되는지 확인
![image](https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/assets/162946806/f81da19d-bdf3-4167-862e-75e298968e1e)
![image](https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/assets/162946806/e970009e-c816-4d33-bd1f-2d291935a329)
- 추후 이 slider index 를 통해 volume image 유연하게 변경 예정
Comment 3 | author: hsskia | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 13 | url: https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9#issuecomment-2033337461
### 해결 과정 6
- UI 에서 할당한 button 의 `onClick` 이벤트에 `RemoveAllListeners` 함수를 적용해도 의도대로 remove 되지 않음
- Button 이 instantiate 되면 원하는 button 의 `onClick` 에만 `AddListener` 를 적용
- 기본적으로 UI 에서 onClick 이벤트에 해당하는 함수를 할당하지 않고 **script** 에서 `AddListener` 로 적용
- UI 에서 접근할 필요가 없기 때문에 **private** 으로 onClick 이벤트 선언 가능
- **Script 에서 control 할 수 있는 것들은 UI 가 아닌 script 에서 해결하자**
Comment 4 | author: hsskia | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 11 | url: https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9#issuecomment-2036202478
### 해결 과정 9
- nrrd file download 가 완료된 후에 nrrd 에 접근해야 에러가 나지 않는다.
- [해결 과정 8](https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9#issuecomment-2034015209) 에서는 download 를 기다리기 위해 Task.Delay 함수를 사용했지만, `StartCoroutine()` 동기 처리 방식을 제대로 이해했다면 이러한 대기 시간은 불필요하다.
```csharp
if (!File.Exists(volumeFile))
{
StartCoroutine(GetVolumeData(seriesId, volumeFile));
}
ShowVolumeImage(volumeFile);
```
```csharp
IEnumerator GetVolumeData()
{
...
yield return ....
...
File.WriteAllBytes(...);
}
```
- 위의 코드에서 `File.WriteAllBytes()` 함수가 사용되기 이전에 `yield return` 이 이루어졌기 때문에 `ShowVolumeImage()` 가 `File.WriteAllBytes()` 보다 먼저 실행되어 file 이 없다는 error 가 발생할 수 있다.
- 따라서 `ShowVolumeImage()` 는 `File.WriteAllBytes()` 이후에 실행되도록 `GetVolumeData()` 의 `File.WriteAllBytes()` 밑에 추가한다.
Comment 5 | author: hsskia | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9#issuecomment-2038651949
### 해결 과정 10
- Dicom image viewer 를 처리하는 부분이 DicomTableview script 에서 많은 부분을 차지
- tableview 와 imageview 는 다른 기능이기 때문에 두 기능을 분리
- tableview와 imageview 는 다른 기능이지만 결국 imageview 도 tableview 와 연동되어 같은 UI 상에 표현되기 때문에 tableview 에서도 imageview 의 함수들을 사용해야 함
### Issue
- imageview script 를 작성하고 tableview 에서 imageview 에 있는 함수나 object 에 접근하려고 하면 `NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object` error 발생
- 단순히 선언만 하는 것이 아닌 `FindObjectOfType<script name>();` 함수로 다른 script 에서 사용한 obejct 를 매칭할 수 있도록 해야함
- `FindObjectOfType` 은 scene 에 있는 objects 중 script 에서 정의한 type 과 일치하는 objects 중 하나를 매칭
- imageview 가 할당 된 obejct 는 volume image 와 slider 를 담고 있는 `volume content` 라는 object 하나 이기 때문에 `FindObjectOfType` 으로 찾을 수 있다.
```csharp
imageViewer = FindObjectOfType<DicomImageViewer>();
```
Comment 6 | author: hsskia | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/hsskia/unity_task/issues/9#issuecomment-2044232827
### 해결 과정 11
- 중복으로 생성해야하는 object 를 항상 scene 에 배치해둘 필요는 없음
- 원본 object 를 asset 으로 가지고 있다면 scene 에 존재하지 않아도 필요할 때마다 복사하여 생성 가능
- 당장 사용하지 않는 object 를 invisible 상태로 두는 것보다 필요할 때 생성되도록 하는 것이 더 가독성이 좋고 효율적인 방법
- 동일한 기능을 수행하는 object 에 같은 task 를 적용하고 싶을 경우
- 원본 object 에 적용하여 다른 object 에도 결과가 반영되게 할 수 있음
-> 위와 같은 문제를 해결하기 위해 object 를 asset 화 하여 재활용이 가능하게 한 prefab 을 사용할 수 있다.
```csharp
newVolumeContent = Instantiate(volumeContent, canvas.transform);
DicomImageViewer imageViewer = newVolumeContent.GetComponent<DicomImageViewer>();
```
-> Instantiate 로 prefab 을 생성하고 특정 script 와 연동하여 사용할 수도 있음

# Latest version throws error, wont allow world to load. Reverting to .15 everything is OK.

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/68

**Describe the bug**
* When loading game with .16 version, this error is thrown and the world fails to l,oad.
```
[Error : Unity Log] 09/11/2023 16:21:31: Exception while loading world C:/Users/Tim/AppData/LocalLow/IronGate/Valheim/worlds_local/HRPlaythrough.db:System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
at XPortal.Patches.ZDOMan_ConnectPortals.Postfix () [0x000f8] in <de0320a6adfa41e6b474e1fd8a07f9bc>:0
at (wrapper dynamic-method) ZDOMan.DMD<ZDOMan::ConnectPortals>(ZDOMan)
at (wrapper dynamic-method) ZDOMan.DMD<ZDOMan::Load>(ZDOMan,System.IO.BinaryReader,int)
at ZNet.LoadWorld () [0x000cf] in <447b19510f604ca3807cd6cce3a7c1ef>:0
```
**To Reproduce**
* Installed latest update via Thunderstore and trioed to load the world I had saved last night with ver .15
**Expected behaviour**
- Expected to load up world with new .16 version of XPortal
**Version**
* 1.2.16
**Environment**
Choose from the following options where you are experiencing the problem (leave only the ones you know about):
* Singleplayer
**Priority**
* High
* ...I reverted to .15 and the world loads fine.
**Additional information**
* Also using Randy Knapps 'Advanced Portals'
* Ver .15 had an issue where every time I would log out, anything other than vanilla wood portals would no longer show up in XPortal and the portals themselves would have no name and no destination. I had to manually set them each play session.
Selected solution comments:
Comment 1 | author: SpikeHimself | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/68#issuecomment-1714599360
Hi @kmGaijin thank you for reporting this.
Could you download the Debug release, enable Debug Logging, and then show me the error again with those?
You can find the Debug release here: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/releases/download/v1.2.16/XPortal-debug-v1.2.16.zip
You can find a guide to enabling debug logging here: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/resources/wiki/BepInEx:-Enable-debug-logging
This way the error in your log file will be more verbose and hopefully help me find the cause.
p.s. you can just drag your LogOutput.log file onto your comment -- it will attach the file
Comment 2 | author: SpikeHimself | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/68#issuecomment-1714634598
Regardless, I have a rough idea of why XPortal crashes. I created a new debug release, please test using this:
[XPortal-debug-1.2.17-issue68-01.zip](https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/files/12580664/XPortal-debug-1.2.17-issue68-01.zip)
Please note that this version stops the game from crashing (at least, that's the aim), but it does not take away the root cause of the error. I don't know what that is, and I don't think it's related to XPortal.
When the game loads, XPortal fetches a list of all the portals in your world, so that it can restore their connections. However, in your case, one of those objects has an invalid ZDOID (that's the unique identifier that the game uses). This should be impossible in normal cases, and so my guess is that another mod is creating an issue at an earlier point.
Comment 3 | author: kmGaijin | association: NONE | reactions: 2 | score: 6 | url: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/68#issuecomment-1714634617

Comment 4 | author: SpikeHimself | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/68#issuecomment-1714638533
Hi @kmGaijin, please ignore my previous comment, it was largely incorrect (your new logfile contained the information I was looking for!).
This new debug version should fix it, please let me know if that is the case:
[XPortal-debug-1.2.17-issue68-02.zip](https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/files/12580682/XPortal-debug-1.2.17-issue68-02.zip)
Comment 5 | author: SpikeHimself | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/68#issuecomment-1714657151
Hi @kmGaijin thanks for confirming, I will create a new hotfix release based on this ASAP. Thank you very much for your assistance and swift replies!
> Where does XPortal store Portal name and destination info?
They are stored in the ZDO object using custom properties. The name/tag is stored in the "tag" property (equal to vanilla behaviour), the destination is stored in the custom "XPortal_TargetId" property.
These values are saved into your world file, this is done automatically by the game itself.
https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/blob/a1203c6d40ca344523c2702d02fc0e4ca1c782eb/XPortal/RPC/ServerEvents.cs#L40-L43
> This is what I'm getting now.
> https://i.imgur.com/6JDq98h.jpeg
The weird text you're seeing suggests that the translation files didn't load. I can indeed confirm that your logfile does not mention them. This is most likely a result of you removing the original XPortal release and replacing it with the debug release (which ships without the translation files).
I'll finish up the 1.2.17 hotfix and I'll tag you again here when it's available. Give me a few minutes :)
Comment 6 | author: SpikeHimself | association: OWNER | reactions: 0 | score: 10 | url: https://github.com/SpikeHimself/XPortal/issues/68#issuecomment-1714669685

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/firebase/firebase-unity-sdk/issues/427

### Please fill in the following fields:
Unity editor version: 2019.3.13 and 2019.3.14
Firebase Unity SDK version: 6.13 and also 6.14
Source you installed the SDK (.unitypackage or Unity Package Manager): Both
Firebase plugins in use (Auth, Database, etc.): Auth, Database, Storage
Additional SDKs you are using (Facebook, AdMob, etc.): None
Platform you are using the Unity editor on (Mac, Windows, or Linux): Mac
Platform you are targeting (iOS, Android, and/or desktop): Desktop/Standalone Windows build throw this error but Standalone Mac build works fine.
Scripting Runtime (Mono, and/or IL2CPP): Mono
### Please describe the issue here:
(Please list the full steps to reproduce the issue. Include device logs, Unity logs, and stack traces if available.
Give a project name with special characters like ç,ü,ö,ı,ğ then
1. Import EDM4U Package from Firebase.com
2. Import Firebase packages with package manager. Start with FirebaseAppCore Package and then Auth, Realtime, Storage
3. Try play mode on editor and works fine.
4. Build for Windows x86_64
5. Start the exe file
What I tried
1. Import EDM4U from firebase/quickstart-unity#641 issue but it does not help.
2. Update Unity version 2019.3.13 to 2019.3.14
3. Create new project then import projects assets and then import firebase packages
4. Search for other related issues
Nothing helps!. Any ideas ?

Comment 6 | author: eAi | association: NONE | reactions: 2 | score: 12 | url: https://github.com/ably/ably-dotnet/issues/764#issuecomment-902919236
I think that the underlying issue that started this whole thread off - and the issue with the broken deserialisation is all caused by stripping. Adding IO.Ably to our link.xml seems to resolve both these issues.
I suggest you include this in your unitypackage (you can have multiple link.xml files, Unity will merge them together).
```
<linker>
<assembly fullname="IO.Ably" preserve="all" />
</linker>
```
There is probably a more subtle way to do this - perhaps preserving the whole assembly is unnecessary and a few necessary types required for deserialisation can be preserved instead.

# Method not found: 'Void System.__Canon..ctor(IntPtr)

- Source: github_issue
- URL: https://github.com/BepInEx/Il2CppInterop/issues/73

MelonLoader v0.6.0 ALPHA Pre-Release
Game Name: TheLongDark
Unity Version: 2021.3.6f1
Game Version: 2.06
Using Il2CppInterop Version = 1.4.3-ci.244
The following exception occurs when trying to either
```
string text = "";
Il2CppTLD.Serialization.SerializationUtils.TryDeserializeObject<string>("some test text here", out text);
-----------------------------------------------
string text = "";
SaveGameSlots.TryLoadDataFromSlot<string>(SaveSlotName,"KeyToGet", out text);
```
```
System.MissingMethodException: Method not found: 'Void System.__Canon..ctor(IntPtr)'.
at Il2CppTLD.Serialization.SerializationUtils.TryDeserializeObject[T](String text, T& result)
```
It was suggested to me that it's a potential problem with **new T(intPtr2)** in
```
[CallerCount(6)]
[CachedScanResults(RefRangeStart = 1397578, RefRangeEnd = 1397584, XrefRangeStart = 1397567, XrefRangeEnd = 1397578, MetadataInitTokenRva = 0L, MetadataInitFlagRva = 0L)]
public unsafe static bool TryDeserializeObject<T>(string text, out T result)
{
System.IntPtr* ptr = stackalloc System.IntPtr[2];
*ptr = IL2CPP.ManagedStringToIl2Cpp(text);
byte* num = (byte*)ptr + checked((nuint)1u * unchecked((nuint)sizeof(System.IntPtr)));
System.IntPtr intPtr = IL2CPP.Il2CppObjectBaseToPtr(System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.As<T, Il2CppObjectBase>(ref result));
*(System.IntPtr**)num = &intPtr;
System.IntPtr exc;
System.IntPtr obj = IL2CPP.il2cpp_runtime_invoke(MethodInfoStoreGeneric_TryDeserializeObject_Public_Static_Boolean_String_byref_T_0<T>.Pointer, (System.IntPtr)0, (void**)ptr, ref exc);
Il2CppException.RaiseExceptionIfNecessary(exc);
System.IntPtr intPtr2 = intPtr;
System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.As<T, object>(ref result) = ((intPtr2 == (System.IntPtr)0) ? ((T)null) : new T(intPtr2));
return *(bool*)IL2CPP.il2cpp_object_unbox(obj);
}
```
"System.__Canon is an implementation detail related to the way generics are implemented in the CLR"
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16854393/strange-system-canon-exception
Please let me know if i can provide any other information or test anything,
Dom (STBlade)

Comment 6 | author: Kasuromi | association: MEMBER | reactions: 0 | score: 15 | url: https://github.com/BepInEx/Il2CppInterop/issues/73#issuecomment-1430727867
You should use the managed `string` type instead of `Il2CppSystem.String`.
Il2CppInterop only considers the managed `string` type when invoking methods at runtime and the only exception to this is field injection I believe.
